Dose: 2 gummies

Active Ingredient: Vitamin C as ascorbic acid, 80 mg per gummy.

Other Ingredients: Maltitol syrup, maltitol, purified water, pectin, starch acetate, natural orange flavor, citric acid, trisodium citrate, B-carotene (color), glazing agent (carnauba wax and vegetable oil), DL-malic acid.

PROS

1. The gummies are fresh.
2. They are sugar-free, if that is something you desire.
3. They are vegan, using pectin instead of gelatin.
4. The additional ingredients are basically safe, though not particularly healthy.
5. All gummies are easier to take than swallowing pills.

CONS

1. These gummies are an extremely expensive way to supplement with vitamin C. The dose is very small at only 80 mg per gummy. Most health conscious individuals who supplement with vitamin C prefer to take at least 500 mg per day.

I saved some extra dirty clothes so I could test this AmazonBasics laundry detergent. A pair of jeans worn while weeding, a polyester Polo shirt and cotton cargo pants worn while lugging greasy, oily, filthy auto parts around. To really put it to the test I threw in an old pair of Privo sandals used strictly for yardwork which had disgustingly ground in dirty insoles despite many washings over the years.

I used a warm water with 1 rinse setting and high spin on my LG front loader. Everything came out spotlessly clean with no pre-treating or rubbing. The sandals looked like new - perfectly white, clean insoles. Wow!

I was surprised at how watery this detergent is. For a top loader it suggests using 1/2 to 3/4 ounce, which is less than suggested by some name brand HE detergents.

Though not unscented, there is almost no fragrance once out of the dryer. For some that's fine, for others well....use a scented dryer sheet or a scent booster in the wash cycle.

I see no reason to use a more expensive name brand detergent when this AmazonBasics detergent does a great job for less money.

The optional strap that comes with it seems sturdy enough. I have it attached though I don't often find myself using it. I like that I can take it off if I find it irksome.

The interior has 3 slots for bank cards (or whatever) as well as a longer slot for paper money. As with every wallet case I have ever had, the opening isn't long enough to just slide money into. I always have to fold it. Not a problem as I usually just carry a little extra cash, and leave my wads of money (lol) for my actual wallet.

The magnetic closure is sturdy and solid. It grabs the case and keeps it closed. Easy to open as needed.

Built in kick stand is basically just allowing the phone to rest horizontally on the inside cover. It works.

I am so impressed by the color that I want the other two colors as well, just to swap out.

The cut-out around the rear camera is perfect. Zero issues. No haziness or other obstruction.

If you are a fan of wallet style phone cases AND use it to hold bank card in the slots, then you should also get a screen protector. I say this because on my 3XL with another wallet case, the cards began to etch the screen. I don't think it is a matter of the brand of wallet or the quality, just the reality of a hard card hitting the screen over and over. So I made sure to buy a screen protector this time around. Now if there is any scratching, it will be on the protector and not the actual phone.

For what it is worth, I like the wallet style not so much for the wallet part, but that it adds an extra level of protection that a non wallet/cover style case offers. I just prefer to have my phone covered from all sides. The interior of the case has the part that holds onto the phone, and it does so well. But I like the wallet aspect too. I tend to just go into the store with my phone rather than bring in a purse. So... No complaints!

I've owned an inexpensive fabric shaver for many years, and although I couldn't exactly call it perfect, it did a really good job, all things considered. However, with the added burden of my son's school uniforms, it had been getting a little finicky, going on strike more often than not, clogging too easily and taking much too long to do the job. (I should add that the aforementioned uniforms are made from the material from hell, which seems to grow pills out of thin air until every square inch of surface resembles coarse sandpaper.)

So there I was, struggling along with shaver and brush, until one day I decided to retool my arsenal, and treat myself to some new firepower. After looking at all the models available on-line at this site, I settled on this one based on brand name, appearance and the reviews. Here's my report:

1. Appearance - Cool and modern looking, with a nice big cutting area and a big fat sliding on-off switch. A large transparent plastic receptacle catches oodles of lint.

2. Ease of operation - the easy grip handle is okay for smaller hands like mine, but I can see that people with large hands and fingers would have a hard time holding this shaver comfortably.

3. Price - Extremely affordable

4. Performance - This shaver is fast and gets the pills off quickly. Emptying the receptacle is easy, and so is putting in the batteries. The instructions suggest that you use only alkaline batteries and not the heavy duty ones. I used two high quality alkaline AA batteries, and was amazed by the speed and power of this little gizmo. Unfortunately, I think I gave it too much juice, because from time to time when it got hold of a particularly large and deeply-rooted pill, it also excavated a tiny chunk of material with a loud "thwack" sound. I subsequently replaced the batteries with a cheaper, less powerful brand, and even though it still occasionally bit too deeply, it was much easier to operate without damaging the fabric.

Points to note:

1. Try it out on a small piece of fabric first. This product is not recommended for angora wool or textured knits et al. It's also not so good with thin polyester/cotton blends or cheap knits (like low quality polo shirts), but works well on twills and similar materials.

2. Make sure the fabric is laid out smoothly, preferably on a flat surface. Wild swipes with the shaver at areas of bunched-up cloth will result in the dreaded "thwack" sound and the loss of a little piece of cloth.

3. Read the instruction manual - it's in understandable English

4. Use inexpensive batteries which have less power than the ones that keep going and going.

Overall, I'm pretty satisfied with this fabric shaver. It cuts fast and is very efficient in sucking up the lint and catching it in the receptacle, but one little slip on your part and those little holes will appear out of nowhere. Once you get the hang of it, I'm sure that you will find that this is another hand held battery operated toy that you can't do without.

Amanda Richards, April 27, 2007

After my last waffle maker had seen better days, it seemed this Belgian Waffle Baker had some pretty good reviews.

I also liked the "flip" style and the sleek design looked easy to store in a smaller kitchen. The truth is, the waffle maker also sits upright on its side and can sit on your counter out of the way until needed. I love the upright storage feature.

The cool-touch handle will warm slightly while you are baking an entire batch of waffles, however it never gets too hot to touch. You may want to keep a mitt nearby incase you feel it is too hot to hold the handle. Steam also escapes from the unit, so watch for steam when turning the baker. You don't actually have to flip the baker, but you can for fluffier waffles.

The green light turns on when the baker is ready and well heated. This item also comes with a small Waffle Baker Recipe Book with recipes for everything from Whole Grain Waffles to Gingerbread Waffles. You can start with a mix or make the waffles from scratch. Most waffle recipes can be used in any waffle baker, so feel free to try your own favorite recipe. I used my Buttermilk recipe and they were delicious.

Sample recipes:

Chocolate Dessert Waffles
Easy Cake Waffles
Banana-Pecan Waffles
Cornbread Waffles
Applesauce Waffles with Sausage Gravy

The main feature you will love is the superior nonstick finish. Nothing sticks and you never have to worry about how you are going to extract the waffles from the baker. They slide out, no problem. While the waffle baker can't be taken apart for cleaning, it was easy to wipe the baker clean once it had cooled completely. Here is my secret Seasoned with Love recipe for delicious Buttermilk Waffles:

Buttermilk Waffles

These waffles are decadent when served with boysenberry syrup, strawberries, whipped cream and confectioners' sugar. I prefer using all-purpose flour from King Arthur Flour. Sometimes I make my own applesauce and serve these hot with warmed applesauce and a drizzling of maple syrup and fresh cream.

2 large egg whites
2 large egg yolks
1/4 cup granulated sugar
3 cups low-fat buttermilk
1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted
2 teaspoons vanilla extract
1 teaspoon extra dry white vermouth
3 cups unbleached all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon baking powder
1 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon baking soda
Corn or canola oil

Set a Belgium waffle baker on to heat. In a deep medium bowl, beat the egg whites to stiff peaks. Whites will have tips that stand when the beaters are lifted. In a large bowl, beat the yolks and sugar. Then, add the buttermilk, butter, vanilla and vermouth.

Sift in the flour, baking powder, salt and soda. Beat for 1 minute, then gently fold in the egg whites. If desired, use a pastry brush to apply a thin coat of oil onto the inside of the heated waffle baker. Ladle a 1/2 cup of batter into the middle of each section and then spread batter evenly.

Close the lid and bake for at least 6-8 minutes.

Strawberries tossed with boysenberry syrup and cream makes a delicious topping. We also sprinkle them with confectioners' sugar.

~The Rebecca Review

Being constantly on the go has made me reluctant to buy a real bed. I've been on beds that are either portable or easy to disassemble like futons for the past 20 years. But I've finally settled down some and need a comfortable place to sleep, especially since I'm getting older. So enter the convenience of shopping on Amazon and a ton of reviews research over a period of a couple of weeks. A couple of caveats for you. I'm not overweight, I don't have back problems, I sleep soundly, and I'm generally considered to be average. I'm also single and not in need of any features for "extracurricular" nocturnal-like activities... just sleep.

I was really looking for something queen-sized, inexpensive, convenient for a 3rd floor apartment dweller with no roommates. I started the research on an inexpensive metal bedframe I could assemble myself that stood tall per my personal preference. Then I got into the mattresses. Let's get into the review:

Pros:
- Super convenient delivery method. The box was about 70 lbs but I was able to carry it myself. Sure I wrestled with it some but it didn't cause any problems. The package came with a letter opener, which really is the ONLY way to open this package, which in my zealous excitement I did incorrectly. I cut all the way down to the mattress. I should have cut more shallow so I could unroll the mattress before decompressing the vacuum sealed part. But since I read a lot of other reviews I was careful and ready for the thing to explode out of the bag and knock me out in the process. It did less so because I went slowly and I kept my face out of the trajectory of the unraveling.
- It was ready to go the same evening I put the bedframe together and took out the mattress. It took another day or so for the pillowtop to rise but it was fine the first night. By the 2nd evening the top felt like it firmed up and I never felt any springs through the top.
- I didn't notice any strong smells. Maybe very very slightly but the metal bedframe had more smell than the mattress and it was negligible. It's been a few weeks now and I don't smell anything from the bed. And never did.
- I don't notice any significant collapsing on the edges like some of the other reviews mention but I don't really sit on the edge of the bed much. There isn't much "sidewall" on this mattress structure wise so you can feel the springs through the side of the mattress but this hasn't been a problem at all.
- On my back and on my belly it seems to support reasonably well and on my side it supports just right. I wouldn't call this firm at all, not in the least. I'd say it favors more toward plush but I really think those terms tend to apply more to beds that bias towards being flat as they're legacy terms that were used before beds were constructed this way. I want to say more that this adapts to the body shape well while being supportive and not feeling like you're falling into the mattress. If you push your fists into the top of the bed however it definitely gives so I'm gonna say this is "plush" of sorts.

Cons:
- I wouldn't do any jumping on this bed. It's not the best idea to begin with but more so this mattress. I think properly cared for it will last a long time but if this mattress is abused (specifically using it as a trampoline) it seems like it wouldn't do as well. At this point I consider this a very minor con as I don't see much practical use in flipping a more classically conventional mattress either. If its of a low quality its going to wear out faster no matter what.

First and foremost, this is a monopod, and should not be expected to perform the duties of a tripod. The two are not on the same playing field, especially if said field is not level, and the monopod's job is simply to hold the fort when a tripod can't go into battle.

Pros:
1. This monopod comes with its own little stand, and is perfectly capable of standing on its own three feet.
2. It can easily support a DSLR with a medium telephoto lens.
3. Set up is simple, requiring only unscrewing the bottom section, opening the legs and screwing the base back on securely.
4. Extends over six feet tall with two adjustable sections
5. Perfect for concert and theatre events in low or changing light, when a tripod either isn't allowed or is impractical.
6. Great for weddings and museum visits
7. You can sit with the monopod braced against your chair and your feet anchoring the legs for extra stability. (I also use a cable release)
8. Padded grip
9. Handy against attacks by stray animals in the wild.

Cons:
1. At the shortest it's still more than two feet long, and doesn't fit well in the external tripod section of smaller camera bags.
2. It's very heavy for all-day trekking around theme parks, museums, big city tours and the like.
3. No carrying case (but has a strap to fasten it on to stuff)
4. Little legs make a lot of noise when concealed (but see below)
5. A bit tricky on uneven ground if you want to use the legs

Things you can fix:
1. Needs a Quick Release head (albeit adding extra weight and cost)
2. Rattling feet can be muffled with a rubber band

Overall, I'm happy with this monopod, except perhaps for the length and weight. It does a great job when you're rushing around in crowded places where tripods fear to tread.

Amanda Richards, June 19, 2013

JARROW FORMULAS SACCHAROMYCES BOULARDII + MOS (30 Veggie Capsules) is a probiotic. Saccharomyces Boulardii is useful for preventing and treating diarrhea (e.g., traveler’s diarrhea), as well as for promoting general intestinal health, and for treating irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), inflammatory bowel disease (IBD, Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis), Lyme disease, and other bowel disorders.

Mannanoligosaccharides (MOS) are nondigestible chains of the sugar mannose, which act as decoys to unfriendly bacteria in the digestive tract. “Bad” microorganisms seeking a long-term foothold in the intestines may bind with the MOS, and get a ride through and out of the system instead.

OF SPECIAL NOTE: Saccharomyces boulardii is yeast (fungus), so it interacts with anti-fungal medications. It's generally safe for adults, but may be dangerous for children or for people with compromised immune systems. It causes gas in some people. The dosage is 1-2 capsules per day. The capsules contain no wheat, no gluten, no soybeans, no dairy, no egg, no fish/shellfish, no peanuts/tree nuts.

This probiotic seems to have no ill effects on me (maybe some extra gas). It seems to help with my IBS (as all probiotics do). My experience with Jarrow products has always been good--it’s a brand that I trust to contain the ingredients the label says the product contains, and to do more or less what the label says the product will do.

This is the 30-capsule travel size. The product is also available in larger sizes that give more value for your money, because the cost per capsule is less.

This review really is for the 4 different Renpure scents i've tried so far: Pomegranate, Coconut cleansing pudding, Rosemary mint and Lavender.

The pomegranate and the coconut both performed well for me. I have pretty thick and textured hair. These both left my hair softened, they left it clean and had no buildup. I have to use quite a bit, maybe 30 pumps or so to get through all of my hair and really work it in, but for the price that really isn't a downside for me. The con of these two is the scent. The pomegranate one is super sweet. When I first smelled it, it kind of put me off. If you like really sweet scents, this might not bother you. To me though, it doesn't smell like pomegranate at all.

The coconut cleansing pudding smelled like straight up Play-doh. I bought two bottles at the same time at TJ Maxx. If I hadn't, it definitely wouldn't have been a re-purchase for me after getting through the first bottle. If you can go locally to smell these for yourself first, I would really suggest that. And then come back to Amazon to order, I can get them for an average of $6.99 a bottle and its about $4 higher in the very few places that actually carry these products.

Now for the other two, the Rosemary mint and the Lavender. I like the scent of both of these. The rosemary mint is just that and its super minty. So if a strong mint scent is your thing, you will probably like it. The Lavender is not a sweet lavender that you would find in a body spray, bubble bath etc... but its a medicinal, natural lavender. Like if you opened a bottle of essential lavender oil, this is what it smells like. Again, a good thing in my book. The negative though is that both for some reason left my hair kind of rough and prone to tangling. I've tried each multiple times and due to that and the burning issue, which I will address next, I may just throw the rest out which is rare for me to not use a product up. These both irritate my scalp quite a bit. I normally work it into my hair first, then wash face and body and rinse it out at the end of the shower. With these two, I start to get a pretty strong burning sensation on my scalp about halfway through the shower. Its not like a refreshing minty tingle either, more of an alarming burn. It does fade of course after some time but its strong enough that I don't want to use the bottles up.

So after using these 4 different scents, I really don't think I will buy any more Renpure products unless I find the coconut one at a super good price. That one performed well enough for me to ignore the funky smell. But the others just have too many negatives to re-buy. One cleansing conditioner that I have purchased multiple times and will continue to re-purchase is the As I Am coconut. It smells good and works great for me.

The setup was easy. Four of the sockets use the backup power, the other four don't. So I hooked up just the necessary things for backup: My PC, monitor, and router. Then I pulled the plug out of the wall. There was no interruption whatsoever - everything just kept running. It said I had 26 minutes of battery time. So I'll break that down, because so many people want a time estimate. I bought the 600va/360w version.

My PC was built to be low power consumption. I estimate it consumes 150w, maximum, and much less when idle. The monitor is a medium-sized 1080p monitor. I am guessing it takes 30w. That's a blind guess. The modem, maybe 15w. So that's less than 200w, and I get 26 minutes running time. Your desktop PC probably uses a bit more power. I'm on a circuit that blows frequently, so I only need a short time while the circuit is reset. So if you're only supporting a router/modem, it should last a very long time. It is apparent to me that many of the unhappy reviewers are need a commercial-grade solution and are expecting much more power and features than this simple, inexpensive UPS has. The unit is rated at 360w. As you approach that maximum, efficiency will drop and your run time will be greatly reduced. Keep it to 200w or less, if you want good efficiency.

Don't try putting a 'fridge or a microwave on this little guy. It isn't made for that. A normal laptop might get a few hours out of this. Most desktop PC's use more power than mine does, especially a fancy gaming rig or software engineer's station. If you have a mighty computer, you won't get much more than time to shut it down gracefully. A more modest computer might last 15 minutes or more. Please keep in mind these are my amateur estimates.

I have had this iPad pillow for 2.5 years, and I'm still very happy with it; however, I ended up making two modifications to make it work better.

Positives:
• lasts a very long time (2.5 years and still going strong with daily use!)
• very comfortable; molds well to my lap or any other surface.
• remains surprisingly clean (dust it as needed; the back fabric hides dust in the foam behind it)
• the foam does NOT collapse after use (still like new after all this time)
• there is still nothing to compare on the market, making this one remain the best choice

Negatives:
• cannot charge iPad easily (must turn it sideways or upside-down OR cram the charger port at the bottom)
• the iPad does NOT stay put - falls off easily (even with its grip strips)
• the bottom hinge comes apart too easily (wish it was full circle or metal)
• too bulky to take "on the go" as it suggests; best to use in one general location (such as different rooms in a house)

Modifications (I'll try to add pictures later):
(1) CUT BOTTOM TO FIT CHARGING CABLE. The first thing I did was use a dremel tool to cut away the middle of the bottom lip which holds the iPad. This allows me to charge the iPad wile still in portrait position without having to turn it upside down or without having the cord smushed up against the lip. Honestly, I'm surprised the manufacturer didn't make this modification themselves after all this time. It's such an obvious improvement and does not compromise any of the other features.

(2) VELCRO TO HOLD IPAD FROM FALLING: The second thing I did was add velcro to hold the iPad so it would stop falling off. I put my iPad in a case and then put a large rectangle of the "soft" side of the velcro on the middle of that case. The large rectangle ensures that the velcro will work in landscape and portrait positions. Then I put two small pieces of velcro on the iPad Pillow. These velcro pieces are the hook side of the velcro and are about 1/2"x1" in size. I put these on the center, moveable part of the pillow. That part has two sections: the top with the Prop 'n Go logo and the bottom which is plain. I put the velcro pieces on the bottom section. They are placed around 1/2" from the top and 3/8" from the edges. The larger the soft velcro on the case, the easier it is to successfully place the hook velcro on the pillow.

Overall, even with the needed modifications, this pillow is still the best iPad lap holder on the market. I can use my iPad while sitting in a chair, relaxing on a couch, sitting on a toilet (you know you do it! LOL), and laying in bed in various positions. It's very comfortable and lasts a long time. Although I wish the hinges were more durable, the plastic used seems to hold up well against normal wear and tear with only a few minor scratches visible when you look up close to find them. If this one should need replacing, I will happily buy another one. It's not perfect, but with so many positives, I highly recommend this Prop 'n Go iPad pillow and give it 5 stars.

I have been using my Omega Vert 330 for about 2 weeks now. In general it is a pretty good juicer. It makes a high quality juice at slow rpm as a masticating juicer should. There is more pulp in the juice than I like, but I solve that with a small strainer. I have no problem with the quality of juice this machine makes. There are however a few problems I have encountered with this juicer so far. A small problem is the strainer basket has to be scrubbed like a son of a gun with a brush to get all of the fiber particles off when cleaning it. So clean up is a bit longer than I would like. I can live with this. The plastic unit that contains auger etc. is hard to get off the motor base. It is awkward to get a hold on and it comes off with difficulty at times. Sometimes I have to bang it with the palm of my hand to loosen it up for removal. I really hate that. The worst thing about this juicer is that fiber strings (from celery, kale stalk, etc) clog up the fiber exit chute every single time. Sometimes it is clogged half way sometimes completely. I think this is a fairly major design flaw. Omega could have either made the opening a little bigger or else made the machine so it chops up these stringy fibers better. Anyway, this is a real problem. The only thing I can think to do is chop up the stems etc. in little tiny chunks before placing them in the juicer. This helps somewhat. Or else don't juice the stems, only the leaf portion. Other than that I think it is a sound juicer. But after using it for a while I think I might have been better served to purchase something different. Oh well, $350.00 spent means I am going to be using this for a while so might as well get used to it.

Wondering why some reviewers say that it doesn't fit the extended battery and others say it works beautifully? Keep reading - I'll explain.

Based on another review, it sounded like this case would work with the Hyperion extended battery, so I bought both and got them today.

The Hyperion extended battery comes with the battery itself and the "extended" back for the phone which curves around to allow space for the larger battery. It looked great by itself, so I then started to put on the Seidio case.

The Seidio case comes with a rubber-like skin that wraps around the phone, and then a harder "skeleton" case that goes around the rubber.

For about 5 solid minutes, I tried to fit the phone into that case without any luck. The curved Hyperion battery back introduces a curve over the camera lens and flash area, but the hard Seidio case is designed to "push" into that area, so it pushes against the battery back and it just won't fit.

The only way to make it fit is to actually LEAVE OFF the battery backing for the Hyperion battery. Once you do that, it fits decently well, and it covers the entire backside of the phone, so the battery case isn't needed. I honestly do not like this one bit. I would much prefer to have both the Hyperion battery cover AND the Seidio case on at the same time. I hate having "leftover" parts for things that I just bought. I knocked off two stars off my rating just for this design - I would have never bought this case if I had known this.

So if you read other conflicting reviews, you'll be able to tell who tried to fit the Seidio case around everything versus the people who left off the battery backing.

I have long very fine naturally blonde hair that I dye A1 (dark blue-black). My hair tends to get dry even though I don't use heat. My hair doesn't accept permanent or semi permanent dyes of any type, a single shampooing drains all the blue tinge out and significantly loses the black. I have tried every color safe, color protective shampoo and conditioner system, and finally accepted this is the way it is and I try to only use shampoo 1-2 x a week max.

I selected this product in the Rich formula.

PROS: It does make my hair healthier and adds moisture. It's nice to have one step and not have to let it sit

CONS: It smells ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE to me - chemical/harsh hair dye/acidic, it does speed up the greasy hair effect for me (second day vs 4th or 5th day), it's very expensive, the pouches are annoying and a waste of plastic, it does tend to make you break out along scalp line/behind ears

I ended up getting the subscription after a few months of use even though I haven't gone through a whole pouch yet, I wanted the lower price and the refillable jar, I just wish they had a more eco-friendly way of getting it to you. I have to use a lot at a time for coverage (long hair, fine hair, and water pH/softness issues) but it lasts a while considering, even if I use it more than 2x a week.

My best method for getting (almost) every drop out is at the end to put it upside down against the side of the shower and running a squeegee (or you can use your hand) and flattening it towards the spout.

If it works for you, I hope you like the smell, thankfully I don't care too much since I work around smelly animals 14+ hours a day and have very limited social life even pre-COVID.

It definitely still makes my hair color run down the drain but it's tied for "best" compared to everything else I've tried.

There are 4 coffee drinkers in my household, and of course we each prefer different coffee types. We enjoyed buying lots of boxes of k-cups, until the novelty wore off and we realized we were paying $.37 to $.66 per cup. That is a whole lot less than stopping and buying a cup on our way to work, but not exactly inexpensive, especially for the one who drinks several cups a day. Buying ground coffee or beans and grinding our own makes each cup $.20 or so. Nice!

Also, throwing all those plastic cups in the trash was getting to our collective conscience. Now we compost the grounds and rinse the cups, putting them through a dishwashing cycle now and then.

You do need to pay attention to how you seal them -- no grounds on the rim, please, and place them carefully, but it sure isn't rocket science and you quickly develop a routine you can do in a caffeine-deprived state. We now have 8 reusable cups and I'll probably get a few more. We can fill them all ahead of time (using colors to indicate which cups hold what) and put them in an airtight canister, which seems to keep them fresh for a few days. We all can definitely manage that for our first cup in the morning!

These are MUCH more economical than the brands I find locally, and work every bit as well.

-Quality yogurt cups cost a minimum of $2.00 each (cheaper than that is only junk like Dannon and Yoplait, which is basically just candy with a few bacteria in it). One cup of good yogurt per day will run you $14 per week. One bottle of Benebiotics will run you $20 for TWO MONTHS.

-Yogurt expires after about a week - maybe two if you get it fresh. Benebiotics "best if used by" date is two years from the date it is packaged.

-A lot of people don't like the taste of yogurt or kefir, but want the benefits they provide. Problem solved.

-People who are dieting may be averse to the fact that yogurt is rather high in calories (quality yogurt is high in fat, and cheap yogurt is high in sugar). Benebiotics: zero calories.

-Yogurt typically has no fiber in it. Benebiotics has 667mg of inulin (natural soluble fiber) per capsule.

Now, on the note of inulin. Some people do react negatively to it, especially until they adjust to it. As many others have stated, if gas seems to be an issue for you, take your daily capsule on and empty stomach right before bed (that's what I do). The chemical reaction is quick, and when it’s done, it’s done, and the water immediately begins to naturally warm to room temperature. You are then left with a rather large bag full of liquid fertilizer of unknown strength. Overall, these may be beneficial for a survival pack, but otherwise, go with a regular ice-pack.

Because it has air in it, it won't feel cool at all where the air is... so it's difficult to get the cold to spread evenly if putting it around something. While it's always best to get your nutrients from natural food sources, sometimes it's not always convenient.

The RDA (US) for zinc for an adult is 11 mg for men & 8 mg for women.

This may not seem like a lot, but if you don't eat shellfish (oysters are the highest at 74 mg per 3 ounces) beef, chicken or pork, then you're left chasing it from lower quality sources like beans, cheese, fortified cereal, etc..

So, in these cases, a supplement may be desired.

These zinc supplements from Vela Nutrition are 50 mg of Zinc Picolinate. This is an easier form of zinc to digest vs other forms.

However, this is a HIGH dose (50 mg) of zinc. For example, if you research higher dose studies (orally) of zinc, the maximum threshold for these higher does is said to be 40 mg.

Always do your own research when deciding on supplements. Especially if you're on other prescription meds or have medical conditions.

While they may seem like just "vitamin pills" there are potential interactions or serious conditions caused by incorrect dosages or the wrong combinations of supplements.

I tried 4 different cases for my replacement Note 8 after the original's screen shattered from a slow drop from 2 feet high in my original case (Incipio Dual Pro). This case had survived many falls/drops/bangs and two of the corner's outer layers had chipped and it was a little slick to hold on to, but in combination with a tempered glass screen protector I thought I was fine. On the fateful day at work I had my phone in my scrub breast pocket, leaned down to get my work bag and it fell out of my pocket, clipped my work bag, and hit the sealed grip flooring (not hard tile or anything) and the screen protect popped off intact and left my phone's screen shattered with chips missing from the bottom left corner. I was devastated even before I then went through 2 weeks of hell through Asurion and received a dud of a refurbished replacement followed by a sketchy second refurbished replacement-replacement. When looking for a new case I was leary of staying with the incipio.

So I purchased 1) UAG (Urban Armor Gear) Plasma Feather-Light Rugged [ICE] Military Drop Tested Phone Case, 2) Unicorn Beetle Shield SUPCASE Full-body Rugged Holster Case with Built-in Screen Protector, 3) Spigen Hybrid Armor Case with Air Cushion Technology and Hybrid Drop Protection, and 4) new Incipio case (Reprieve Sport).

My biggest concerns for the case were corner and screen protection. I ended up returning all of them except the Unicorn Beetle case even though I hated it, because all of the others had varying degrees of poor corner protection (or 3 corners were good but the corner holding the S-Pen was pathetic), and they had almost no lip to prevent the long sides of the phone's screen. None of them worked as well with the tempered glass screen protectors as the original Incipio Dual Pro did (The Unicorn Beetle case has it's own screen protector so isn't used with a separate one unless you modify it to remove the built in one). I have always liked spigen but it was overall just too thin and flimsy for me. The outer grip was one of the better ones but my bigger concern is when the phone is unintentionally OUT of my hand (nearly all my previous phone's falls were NOT from my phone slipping from my hand). I chose the Unicorn Beetle because, again, I think it will protect my phone the best) but it's a pain to use, ugly, and has many annoyances (I don't want to have to use 2 hands to pry the unnecessary port covers off for the jack or charger, it adds a ton of depth dimension to an already big phone, the design aesthetically is poor and looks like everyone else's iphone case to me, and it still doesn't have the perfect S-Pen corner converage as far as the back of the phone goes (but of all these cases it's the best). I'd honestly prefer to have to work and pry my S-Pen out and have that corner protected then not have it protected (and I use my S-Pen all the time).

In summary, this case is not at all attractive to me (everyone at work has a similar looking case for their iphone in different colors). It's bulky and doubles the width of the phone. The built in screen protector is very hard to keep clean (outer surface and inside- lets dust hair, etc inside somehow, and the protector cracked after about a month when it got knocked against a cup holder in the work vehicle. The S-Pen works OK on the screen protector (I'd give it an 8/10 in that regard). The biggest things I hate are the unnecessary port protectors that I'm about to just cut off. I have to use 2 hands to pry them open enough to insert my aux jack each time I get in my car to play audio as well as to plug in the charging port. It actually almost prevents the aftermarket plug from engaging all the way (the plug that came with my replacement Note 8). It's corner protection is OK, still lacking somewhat on S-Pen corner. Where it beat the other cases was it's protection of the long edges of the phone's screen with the top sandwich style case piece. Side button function isn't the crazy effort is is with Otter cases. Another drag is something about the backside of the case makes it less effective with my Spigen magnetic car vent phone mount. With the center raised brand logo section on the back I have to be pretty exact when I set it up on the mount or it slides a bit. It has taken a tumble numerous times despite the fact that this has been the most rock steady strong magnetic mount I've ever seen and have tried 6 other cases with it with never an issue. In fact, it's more likely to pull the whole mount off the vent than separate, except with this case).

Almost 2 months in it's fairly durable against scratches/dings etc, I can see a few faint scuffs on the rubber bumper. The screen protector is another story and looks like crap and it's not like I store it in a purse against keys and a pocket knife or a hedgehog or anything. The corner bumpers were the 2nd thickest that I tried EXCEPT for the S-Pen corner! This was still less than I'd hope for. I know they are stuck between a rock and hard place since many people, especially guys with big thick fingers, complain about S-Pen access, but I'd rather have my phone not shatter and have to work a bit to get my S-Pen out than not (personal preference). Also, as having been dealing with an S-Pen since 2013 with my Note 10.1 2014 edition and my first Note phone- the Note 3, it's not like the S-Pen hasn't gotten easier to get out in general with the assist press.

If you have a rough lifestyle with phones like I do and they drop/fall/bang a lot, you most certainly need at least a tempered glass screen protector in place of the built in screen protector this has, or can cross your fingers and hope it cracks and not your phone with less than serious knocks/falls.

If you care about the long sides of your phone's screen this type of case is for you. It's a good company with well made products and it's not their fault I just don't care for the looks. It took 1st place out of the many cases I've tried but I'll be the first to admit I'm still looking for The One (that protects AND looks good). And I'm definitely chopping off these port covers.

UPDATE: after several months it's going in the trash. Screen protector was so buffed/scratched and corner of case was cracked so I have switched to "Samsung Galaxy Note 8 Cell Phone Case - Ultra Thin Clear Cover with Built-in Anti-Scratch Screen Protector, Full Body Protective Shock Drop Proof Impact Resist Extreme Durable Case, Black/Grey"

I couldn't be happier- all the things that annoyed the heck out of me about the unicorn case (look/feel/bulkiness, sliding off my magnetic phone holder, trapping dust/hair/fuzz UNDER the screen protector and annoyingly difficult unnecessary port-covers are not a problem with this cheaper case. The only difference is that the back outer case is not as thick which will only be a problem if my phone has an impact from a hard/sharp object, not a drop. The grip and feel of this case is way better, I can see the nice color of my actual phone, and edges, screen, and corners are equally protected. I did buy a plain black unicorn supcase as an emergency back up but I am WAY happier with this different case.

I've been sampling a lot of different meal-replacement AKA high-protein bars lately, because I eat a lot of them and I am looking for variety. For me, this bar is a real failure. First and foremost, it is rather dry, and not very sweet. Even though it is supposed to be a "brownie," it only barely resembles one in taste and not at all in texture.

As if all that were not bad enough, this bar is sweetened with maltitol. Sugar alcohols have about 70-90% of the sweetness of white sugar, but the body does not digest them, so manufacturers who include them in their products label them "sugar free." Unfortunately, the fact that sugar alcohols cannot be digested means that they lead to offensive, and often painful, bowel distress. And of all the sugar alcohols, maltitol is the absolute worst for producing these symptoms. Since this is a well-known fact, I can't believe anyone selling a bar marketed as "healthy" would include sugar alcohols. What bothers me, as well, is that there is no gain from the pain of the sugar alcohol--this is a very high calorie bar for such a relatively small one: 230 calories!

I will not be purchasing this bar again.

The package contains 18 round patches, 1” in diameter. The patches have a thick gel on one side which, when applied to a bug bite, provides some instant cooling relief. I’ve used the patches on a few different bites and have found they work, at least for a while.
I do, however, have a couple of issues with them. First, they’re large. Since they’re so large and my bug bite was not nearly that large, I thought I’d cut one in half. Cutting it was easy, but I learned that the smaller the piece, the quicker the patch dries out, gets brittle around the edges, and falls off. Lesson learned. So, that means you probably have only 18 uses in a package, though I did have some success using a smaller piece and covering it with a bandaid to keep it in place. Not ideal, and not what I should have to do, but effective. Maybe these could come in different sizes within a package?
Next, depending where you put the patch, it’s easy for clothing to rub against it and dislodge it sooner than would otherwise happen. The patches are sticky, but I found they’re no match for the waist band of a pair of jeans. Again, maybe the bandaid trick would work in this instance. Unlike a bandaid which can stick and be hard to remove, if you want to remove these patches before they fall off themselves, it’s simple and painless.
Overall, these are effective short-term and are a nice alternative to messy creams.

For example I use a 400 mm machine which requires 30 droplets because the scent is more light and meant to run 6-12 hours. You may need to add 5 or 10 droplets extra into the diffuser to make it more noticeable. But again, it depends on the persons because each person smells things differently.

TIP: most diffusers have a slot where you drop the oil. If you're like me and have one of those it's meant to guide the droplets inside the water but a lot of the times it ends up concentrated in one area or certain oils fail to disburse inside. (This makes the oil/water/diffuser have a delayed effect on scent/smell.) After adding droplets inside, turn it on, and on top of the diffuser there's a hole where the mist comes out, drop the extra 5-10 droplets inside. This concentrates the oil closer to the diffusing section giving the smell a kick start. Later on, the water with the oil you added in the section catches up with diffuser.

I've used Farberware products in my kitchen for at least thirty years. It's good quality kitchenware that usually holds up for years.

This Farberware 12-Piece Cookware set is first and foremost pretty. It's not the heaviest gauge, but it is well made and it's just plain appealing -- especially if you love turquoise, have a turquoise kitchen or have turquoise as your accent color. I also like the ceramic nonstick surface inside for cooking and easy cleanup. You can put this in the dishwasher, but it cleans up well with soap and hot water. The longer you can clean it without abrasives, the longer the ceramic surface will stay new looking. Once the surface is scratched or scuffed with abrasive cleaners (this includes dishwasher soap), it creates pores that allow for deterioration.

When the box states 12-Piece, it's counting the 3-piece, black nylon Prestige tool set -- large spoon, slotted spoon and slotted spatula.

The smallest pan is quite small, perfect for frying an egg, maybe two. At the rim, it's only about five-inches across, and down inside where the food goes, it's about four-inches. This is to help you get an idea of the graduated sizes of the rest of the set -- it's not a huge set. But, it's well made with sturdy handles on the pots and pans and the lids are shatter-resistant glass. The larger skillets have a "quilted" surface for better browning. This is oven safe to 350 degrees.

The turquoise exterior and white ceramic interior is very "upbeat." If you're cooking more than three hundred meals a year, as I have been doing for years, pulling this pretty color out of the cupboard can be motivating.

It would make a lovely gift -- especially for college students. For new cooks, this set combined with James Briscione's, "The Great Cook: Essential Techniques and Inspired Flavors to Make Every Dish Better" would make a spectacular gift package.

Because of this I search for great deals on year old premium smartphones. I previously had a Nexus 6, then when it went kaputski, I got my wife and I a couple of Prime G6+ ThinQ phones in January 2018. They worked fantastically for us for 2 3/4 years before starting to go bad, with the battery life falling apart, errors on the apps, and even the audio jack going bad on mine. Plus, the phone screen was 5.7" which was a disappointing move backwards after two years with our 6" phones.

I looked at all the various phones available, and initially purchased the Samsung A50 for $350. This is a beautiful phone with an amazing 6.4" screen; however, it is not a premium phone. The speakerphone was garbage so I couldn't hear people, based on the mic quality people couldn't hear me on the other side, and the fingerprint reader in the screen was horrible. Since I need my phone to be quick and functional, I had to return it. After that, I seriously considered the Prime G8+ ThinQ, but the yo-yo pricing got me as it went up from $499 to $850 on the day I decided to buy it (SMH). Based on that, and the fact that it still has a 6" screen, a Snapdragon 855, and 6 GB of RAM, I decided to buy the V35 for $399. So far, I have to say I don't regret the decision at all. So, for the good and bad:

Good:
- Speed: With one of the newest top end CPU's and 6 GB of RAM, this phone has sped through everything I've thrown at it.
- Fantastic screen: As expected on a premium device, they'll tell you it's not as good as Samsung, blah blah blah, but for my eyes, it's fine. The only way to really tell the difference is to stare at both screens, which is weird anyways, lol.
- Great battery life: I leave home at 100% and my old phone was at 50% by 10AM, this one is at 45% at 4:30PM when I'm leaving work! This is a HUGE relief, and I often don't plug my phone it at work, or when I go to sleep...so I can live without worrying about constantly charging the phone.
- Smilar Ecosystem: I didn't have to adjust, per owning the G6+, which is big for me. Even though I use Nova Launcher, pulling down from the top and having to find where everything was on the Samsung was a bit irritating to me.
- Audio Experience: I have to say I really enjoy the DAC functionality, as I have my headphones on for much of the day when I'm doing admin work. I'm glad they kept that.
- Price: - $399 for a phone that has top tier specs as of late 2018, is insane
- Speaker Phone: It is LOUD. I'm probably going to buy one for my Dad as his hearing is bad and he doesn't like the speakerphone on his current phone.

Bad
- Wide Phone: Side to side this phone isn't much wider than my G6+ but is far wider than the G8+ and most modern phones. As a guy with medium sized hands, it can be irritating.
- Case Availability: This one got to me. The case availability is horrible. I like a strong case with big edges without built in screens, but they simply don't exist for this. Plus, the cases available are 90% the V20 and V30 ones, which don't fit quite right per a slight change on the back camera, yet still pop up on every search when you are looking.
- Random Screen Dimming: This one is a weird one, but it automatically dims your screen on occasion. I'm sure there is a way to turn this off, but it happens so randomly I forget to look back into it afterwards.
- Bluetooth Connection: Not sure if this is the phone or other items I have, but it doesn't "automatically" connect to available items like my G6 or Nexus 6 did. I have to often select it, even in my car, or with my speakers at home. It still works fine, but it's a weird irritation.

Overall, I'm super glad I got this phone at the price I did. My wife is still waiting for Black Friday to get a Galaxy 10+, (mostly for the camera) but I'm fine with this phone as it does what I need quickly and without issue. Honestly, for half the price of a new Pixel or Galaxy, and $200-$300 less than last generations of both, you get almost as much phone and even a few extra things, like the DAC. If you don't have money growing out of your ears, need a high quality phone, and can't wait until the next Black Friday or Prime Day, I'd say just go ahead and buy this.

Adding phosphatidylcholine does not make it liposomal. Regardless, that additive should enhance bioavailability because fisetin has low oral bioavailability and is not soluble in water. It is rapidly metabolized.

Fisetin is used for clearing out old senescent cells. In a 2018 study, fisetin was the most potent senolytic found out of 10 falvonoids tested. In 2021-2023, it is being actively studied by the Mayo Clinic in humans. Fisetin is found naturally in fruits and vegetables. It has similarities to quercetin.

The dosing of supplemental fisetin is unknown and the benefit in humans is unproven. The Mayo clinic human studies are using 20 mg per kg of body weight, which would be 1.6 grams for an 80 kg (176 pound) adult. These pills have 1.2g of fisetin. This $41 bottle has 60 servings at a cost of $0.68 per serving. Some people experimenting with fisetin are taking 3g per day. Another way to get rid of senescent cells is fasting, which is free.

The health claims made in the marketing regarding these pills increasing brain function, focus, and alertness in humans are unproven and are likely false. Mouse studies do not translate to human effects. I do not notice anything at all from these pills.

Vitamin D3 is the most bioavailable form of vitamin D, which is well known by both alternative and mainstream medical practitioners to have bone-protective properties.

Vitamin D3 comes in several different dosage sizes. The 1000 IU version is versatile in that you can tailor how much you want to take, if you desire to take between 1000-4000 IU per day. If you plan to take 5000 IU per day, Life Extension makes that dosage size as well. I use this particular brand because the company is highly reputable.

There are varying opinions on how much D3 to take. My own alternative healthcare provider has vacillated over the years between recommending a dose of 1000 IU per day, to 2000 IU, to the 5000 IU of this product. I personally take between 1000 - 5000 IU per day depending on the time of year. Regarding a potential danger of overdose of vitamin D, the body itself produces up to 20,000 IU of vitamin D after just 20 minutes of unprotected sun exposure in the summer, with no ill effects. However, for those embarking on a dosage of more than 1000 IU daily, ideally you would do it with a doctor's supervision, having the doctor regularly test your blood levels of vitamin D. Your doctor can test them by ordering a lab to do the 25-hydroxy vitamin D test, abbreviated as "25(OH)D." This is touted as the most reliable test of vitamin D status. Optimal levels range between 50 and 70 ng/mL.

Of course, if you are willing to allow a few minutes of sun exposure in the summer, you can get all the vitamin D you need that way during that time of year. However, in the winter, the angle of the sun is such that if you don't live quite near the equator, the body produces inadequate vitamin D when exposed to the sun--not to mention that very little of the skin is exposed to the sun when it is severely cold outside. Research has discovered that Americans as a whole are dangerously deficient in vitamin D, especially during winter months. The body's ability to produce vitamin D naturally also declines with age.

In addition to its well-known benefit of protecting bones, vitamin D encourages the body to produce substances called cathelicidins which destroy viruses, bacteria, and other microbes, which is why vitamin D increases resistance to colds and flu. Research has shown that people who take cod liver oil lower their risk for respiratory infections of all kinds. (Apparently this 19th Century cure-all actually was a viable home remedy.)

The risks associated with suboptimal blood levels of vitamin D are many, including: high blood pressure, increased cancer risk, metabolic syndrome, diabetes, and obesity. The benefits of supplementation and the risks of deficiencies of vitamin D increase as we age. In particular, in senior citizens vitamin D deficiency is linked with generalized bodily weakness, an increased possibility of developing macular degeneration, and a 2.5 times greater risk of death. In contrast, research has indicated that supplementing with vitamin D decreases the risk of developing cancer of the colon, lungs, and breast. It also improves balance in old people--which is a great thing since older people are at substantial risk of death from a fall. It also improves mood, and as such is a natural treatment for depression (it is well known that depression rates increase in winter due to lesser amounts of sunlight). Studies have shown vitamin D improves symptoms of all kinds of autoimmune disorders such as psoriasis, and that it can relieve the pain of fibromyalgia.

During flu season, vitamin D3 can help keep you from getting sick or lessen the duration of bouts of colds, sore throats or flu. My healthcare provider recommended to me taking as much as 10,000 IU on a day I begin to get a cold or flu. I've been on this supplement for years, along with 2000 IU of vitamin C daily, and haven't had a cold or flu since.

KVM switches are handy for data centers, repair shops, or anywhere there are more computers than monitors/input devices. They tend to be much cheaper than this, but this is no typical KVM.

For starters this comes in an all business brown box devoid of marketing fluff. Folks buy these because they work with a sophisticated sales associate or do their own research (being Amazon, you'll fall into the latter). Inside is an equally serious device. Devoid of any visual frills and exuding robust quality, the relatively compact device is pretty straight forward. As with any KVM you have X+1 set of ports, in this case 4 in plus 1 out (well the keyboard and mouse are inputs). The difference here is that these are not only secured to NSA standards, they're built to handle the highest graphical specifications to allow for high end devices or futureproofing for that eventuality. Typical data center or repair shop scenarios don't usually call for 4k displays, but a high end workstation setup (perhaps with multiple boxes that need time to render or perform other tasks) could definitely use the capacity. No matter your needs, the signal is crisp, clean, and devoid of any artifacts. The available hardware switches are a blessing compared to low end ones that need a weird hotkey setup.

Is this for you? Well I guess it is if you're shopping for $600 KVMs your needs are well above the $30-80 devices you can find elsewhere or even the "higher end" $100-200 ones. Just know that many users would be just as happy to spend 10-20% the cost of this. This is a serious device for advanced users. In that context, and in any other, it delivers. I'd love it to add IP KVM abilities via the unused ethernet port (currently "for future use"), but as is, it's still a remarkable tool for those who have invested thousands in systems and have priceless data.

Interesting product. Thousands of five-star reviews here--way, way more than any other shave soap--and yet, there is nothing exceptional about it. It does build a pretty good lather, with moderate slickness. Lack of scent (or at least lack of strong scent; I guess there is a detectable scent if you get your nose right into it) is also a plus in my opinion. That all said, I don't really see why this product towers above all other shave soaps on Amazon. There are better lathering soaps, slicker soaps, and soaps with stronger or more interesting scents (for those so inclined). For instance, the (less expensive) Tabac blows this one away for lather and slickness; the famous Mitchells Wool Fat has similar lathering to the Cavendish but blows it completely out of the water in terms of shaving slickness and post-shave comfort. Both are sold on Amazon. I am not saying this isn't a good product; I give it an A- / B+ and I don't think it would disappoint anyone (with the possible exception of Tabac users, who are used to explosive lather that the Cavendish doesn't have), I just wonder why thousands of people are declaring this the greatest shave soap ever on Amazon.

In summary: A- / B+ shave soap that is perfectly fine and won't disappoint you, but may not provide the absolutely best achievable lather and slickness.

I purchased 2 of these phone covers for my husband and I and we have both been very happy with how they perform. The case fits the phone very well and does not accidentally slip off. The case is designed so that it wraps around and covers all the edges of the phone, which I like. It also has vertical supports on the bottom of the phone around the lightning port and the speakers/headphone jack (you can see it in the pictures that show the bottom of the phone). The befit to this design is it keeps the bottom edge of the cover that is on the front of the phone in place better. Other covers I looked at that did not have these additional pieces in them allowed the front part of the cover to move up and down off of the edge of the phone, effectively not protecting the bottom edge of the phone. This feature of the cover was a must for me when I was looking for a case.

I have a black iPhone and so the cover looks darker on my phone that it shows in the item pictures. If you have a white phone I'm sure it would look just like the pictures, but be aware that since the cover is semi-translucent that the black will darken the color some. I still really like the color, just not quite as in-your-face pink.

My only complaint for this cover is the opening for the headphone port can be too small for some headphone connectors. The headphones I use have a connector that is straight in and skinny so it fits fine. However the headphone jack for my car is a 90 degree connector and has a bigger footprint and so does not plug in all the way with the case on. To get the headphone to plug in correctly while in my car I have to pop off the bottom corner of the case. Not a deal breaker and I'm not sure there is a lot more they could do within the dimensions of the phone but something to make note of.

Overall a really well designed iPhone 5 case for a very good price.

I had FIOS cable previously, but I cut the cord a while back. Everything was mostly working great, but my wireless throughput isn't the best, and the signal occasionally exhibits extremely high latency -- especially when there are a lot of connected devices.

I wasn't sure exactly how to remedy this problem, until one day I noticed that the two highest-traffic areas, the TV and my home office, both have now-unused coax connectors just sitting there. After researching a bit I found a competitor to this product, which was twice as expensive and didn't work at all. And then I found this.

Installation simply could not be easier. Here's how it went: Box arrived from Amazon. I opened it. I plugged in one of these things in my basement, between the router and the first cable splitter. Went upstairs, plugged a second one in in my office. Turned on my computer. Done. On the network, 4x faster throughput than before, vastly reduced latency.

TV, same thing. I just plugged it in, and it went directly online.

The only minus of this product is that there are, as far as I can tell, no one-packs available. So now I have an extra one sitting around, and nothing left to wire. Or maybe it's a backup unit in case one of them fails. I haven't had this product long, to be honest, so I don't know how long it will last. I'll come back here and update the review when/if one bites the dust.

In any case: So far, very good. I highly recommend this product if you want to bring an ethernet signal through your unused coax.

I previously didn't like the idea behind Pyrex glass blows do to the weight. But I have changed my mind and only buy these now.

The bowls are easy to clean, they don't soak up oil, don't trap smells (the cover can if you leave it closed sitting for a week at room temperature) and don't slowly melt in the microwave. The glass bowls are also easier to clean do to surface regularity, the plastic bowls tend to have indents/grooves for strength so it takes more effort to get food out. The glass is also more transparent than plastic bowls, but this a small point. The square bowls are especially welcome for they don't take up as much room in the refrigerator as the large round mixing bowls or the plastic ones which can deform when over packed.

I have dropped a few out of the freezer, and so far they didn't break. The plastic ones tend to shatter on impact with the floor. Though that's not to say that the glass will not break, it's just that I have not managed to break one yet.

These are my go to container for food storage and lunch for work.

Most people think of screen protection for a mobile phone as a glass or plastic cover that prevents the actual screen from shattering. That’s true, this is the most important aspect of screen protection. But, what about protecting the data displayed on the screen? I have seen privacy screens for laptop screens, but this is the first I have used with a mobile phone and it works exactly like the laptop screen protectors.

Similar to a regular screen protector, this is a thin sheet of glass that applies very smoothly and easily with no bubbles. It has fine screen coverage to the edge of the phone - this has been an issue on some other screen protectors I have used but not this one.

With this screen protector in place, the screen is definitely darker than usual and it might be helpful to adjust the screen brightness. It is a lot like looking at your screen through a pair of sunglasses. Turning the phone at a 45-degree angle makes the screen appear completely black as if the screen has been turned off - no light can be seen at all.

Before I put this protector on the phone I held it up to a light source and saw a repeating pattern of the light source itself, almost like I had held up a mirror to a mirror to get a replicated image. I think this protector works via polarized light and the repeating image is an effect of that - I have seen similar phenomena when wearing polarizing sunglasses.

If protecting the data on your phone screen is as important to you as protecting the screen itself, this is the screen protector you need. It works great, is easy to apply and is sufficient protection for you phone’s screen to prevent physical damage. Just make sure you have the right one for your model of phone.

Years ago when you could still find them on Amazon I bought the highest powered green laser pointer I could find. With new Ultimate Lithium batteries this laser will pop a black balloon. Ok, it takes a while but it'll do it. If you hold both the laser and the balloon rock-solid steady for about 3 minutes. Anyway ...

I ran across this mount and decided the laser would fit it. It works fantastically. Make sure the finder scope cross hairs are correctly zeroed, adjust the laser to point to the intersection of the cross hairs and Bingo! You can now use the laser to get in the vicinity of what you want to see and do your fine adjustment with the finder scope.

This has been so much handier than you would probably think, often with a high powered finder scope you aren't really sure that the thing you're zeroed in on is actually the thing you want to observe. You look through the main tube and find out that it is or it isn't. Now I can get close enough that there's no doubt when I look through the finder, you can actually see the laser beam in the finder.

I love this because I have an Orion 10 inch Dobsonian Intelliscope. You have to precisely target two known stars to orient the Intelliscope feature. It doesn't really care which stars, so I use Polaris and Mizar (the middle star in the "handle" of the Big Dipper) because those are very easy to find and always visible at night where I live. Using the laser cuts down my orienting time to almost nothing so I can get on with my observations.

This would all work exactly the same way with a powered "Go To" mount, you have to orient those in exactly the same manner only with some you have to use 3 stars instead of 2 stars.

Not to mention that the great big tube of the Orion sitting there spitting a green laser beam at the sky looks very cool too. I didn't do this for the "cool" factor, that's a bonus.

I also have a Telrad finder and that's very handy too. With the three finders I never have a problem getting my telescope pointed where I want it.

There is one downside to using a laser. I live near an NAF (U.S. Naval Air Field) and seriously you'd better be absolutely sure that you don't point that green beam at any aircraft. Not even CLOSE to any aircraft. Those boys can see that beam as well as you can and if they think you're pointing it at them you're going to get a visit from a black SUV carrying people with no sense of humor at all. Lasers can blind a pilot momentarily and while it's been a long time since I was in the military it wouldn't surprise me a bit if it sets off inbound tracking alarms in the cockpit too. So be exceedingly careful about where you point your laser.

I use mine for orienting the scope, and finding my next target. I shut it OFF when I'm not actively using it. This saves batteries (those Lithium batteries are expensive) and saves on the beam generator in the laser, extending it's life. Once you use a laser like this you won't want to set up your scope without it.

I evaluated this along with another device for left ear use only in which I have a mild to moderate high frequency loss. I am using it with the "open" ear piece. For the LifeEar, what resulted in my keeping it after evaluation is the following: (1) Program 2 is designed for my hearing loss and is very helpful. Whereas Program 1 is useful too and I am still experimenting between the two. A particular situation I found important was the ability to turn up the volume in a church setting to hear my preacher better, which works well without introducing squealing or feedback. That should be useful in other large room settings. (2) In some noisy restaurant situations, Programs 3 and 4 help a bit. I suspect they would help even more if I used the "closed" ear piece, but from past hearing aid experience I know I like the open ear piece better than closed. In other noisy restaurant situations, it doesn't help at all, and I think the difference is that noisy talkers are too close to me verses more dispersed. (3) Unlike my most recent hearing aid which the LifeEar replaced, I am a music lover and the LifeEar doesn't reduce the quality of that sound. (4) This device is better for me than the four year old prescription, multi-channel aid that I recently lost. And in particular, being able to change the volume setting is most useful which I could not do with the older aid.

Here is what could be improved which is why I deduct the 5th star: The battery is very small and hard to insert. When I open the battery compartment slightly to turn off the aid, it battery often falls out in my pocket carry case. As compared to the other device I evaluated, the volume/program switch is a little smaller and a bit harder to manipulate. In noisy situations where I might try different programs to see if I can make an improvement, I can't hear the beeps to let me know if I have changed a program and to which program.

Overall, I am very happy with the LifeEar. But given that you can try at least some of these aids during an evaluation period, you may want to try more than one.

This is a gel-like liquid clog buster that is less smelly and more septic-friendly than the traditional lye-based clog busters. Unfortunately, it's also less effective. It does work, but you need to use a large amount and give it overnight to see any measure of results. The recommended dose for sinks/tubs/showers is 16 oz, with a second application recommended for difficult obstructions. For toilets the usage amount is 32 oz. While the gallon looks like it would last for some time, you can run through it pretty quickly.

It did work for me in a bathroom sink clog. It's mostly a hair clog, and I usually clear it by removing the trap and cleaning it out manually. Granted, using this gel was way less work and mess but it did take 2 doses to get the drain running again.

There's no info on the bottle with regard to ingredients, but there's an SDS (Safety Data Sheet) available on the manufacturer's website. While this is less corrosive than a conventional clog buster, it still is corrosive, especially for metals. The instructions recommend not using it for finished surfaces, coated metals, aluminum, marble, granite, quarts or other stone surfaces. The manufacturer also recommends wearing gloves when using this.

I applaud the effort to provide a less corrosive clog approach, but the lackluster performance and the large amount needed per use puts my rating at three stars (average). It's not something I'd get again to clear out a clog.

The Deco 3 has, for the most part, been rather enjoyable to use. The 6 hotkeys and scroll wheel offer the perfect amount of custom functionality, while the active drawing area is adequate yet still compact and portable. The pen has a great feel in the hand, and that it doesn't require batteries or need to be recharged has been a convenience for sure. Sensitivity levels are amazing, though I have found myself decreasing the range to accommodate my own pressure preferences. My favorite feature, however, is the wireless capabilities...so nice just to set back and draw without a tether. All in all, the tablet functions above my expectations for the price point and I feel it was a good purchase.

BUT, I have two issues...one major, one more of an annoyance. First and foremost, the driver USB provided by XP-Pen comes preloaded with a virus called Win32/Ramnit.A - something company reps will tell you over and over is no big deal, will not impact your system, can just be ignored and to simply format the flash drive. Their solution is to go to the website to download the current drivers, which should always be done regardless...but for a company to send out an infected component, claim that it's a false-positive when it is not (many people in numerous countries using various virus software have all received the same warning), and to brush off the implications of such is highly irresponsible. Note...this is the FIRST thing you experience when you purchase this tablet and go to use it, so it's far less than a favorable first impression. I resisted leaving a review immediate upon purchase based on this issue alone, instead opting to put the tablet through its paces.

Concern/annoyance #2 is the replaceable pen tip inserts. The plastic used is fairly durable and doesn't wear down too fast, but faster than I would have expected. The annoyance, however, is that they have inclusions which turn a very smooth drawing experience into an abrasive one. I thought maybe it was just an issue with the first tip I used, so I switched it out...same result. Switched out to a third tip...same result. Am on my fourth tip now and the inclusions persist. Being that this is the point of contact and dictates the tactile drawing experience, the feeling of dragging a grain of sand across your tablet is awful. I've found that I can temporarily 'remedy' this abrasive contact by very, very lightly rolling the tip on a 600 grit diamond surface, bringing the tip back to a smooth finish and feel. However, after a few hours of usage the plastic has once again worn down just enough to expose the inclusion and results in the abrasive feel again. This process, of course, causes additional wear on the tip and I expect to have to purchase a new set of tips within the next few months. I'm hoping the inclusion issue has been resolved by that time...

Verdict: Good tablet for the price, functions well, overall happy with the purchase...but -1.5 stars for the Win32/Ramnit.A issue and how the company has responded to customer concerns, and -0.5 stars for the abrasive inclusions in the replaceable tip material.

PROS

1. This product offers two pairs of identical scissors, except that each has a different color handle. This distinction allows you to, if so desired, delegate each pair of scissors for a distinct function, such as storing one pair with your garden tools and the other pair in the kitchen.
2. These scissors have sharp, serrated edges, and each pair comes with its own protective sheath.
3. These scissors worked well when I tested them for cutting paper, thick plastic, thin cardboard, and plant stems. They also worked great for mincing fresh herbs, such as basil, mint, and parsley.
4. These scissors offer a bottle opener built into their blades.
5. The grip on these scissors is comfortable and non-slip.
6. The price is quite reasonable.

CONS

1. I think advertising these scissors as being both durable and sharp enough to take on the task of cutting up meat, poultry and raw vegetables, versus using a knife and a cutting board, is too ambitious for them. Even if they were capable of those cooking tasks, I wouldn’t personally consider using scissors that way for fear of breaking apart their hinge.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

I would not personally recommend running these scissors through the dishwasher. After I use them in my garden, I wipe them off with a damp cloth first to remove sap and debris, then wipe them with a dry cloth to remove all moisture, before returning them to their sheath and putting them away. In the kitchen, after using them to cut up herbs, I wash them by hand and dry them well with a soft, cotton towel before putting their protective sheath back on them and storing them in a drawer

When you’re on the go and need to keep your items organized when you step into the shower, a shower caddy is a must. You just hook the caddy in place and everything you need is right there, within easy reach. A practical caddy for the task is this 7 Pocket Shower Caddy Tote from the Handy Laundry Store.

Most shower caddies I have used have been made from metal/wire. These are still my preferred type of caddy for my home. But for travel and other times when you need to be mobile with your caddy, a product like this is better. It is made utilizing a mesh design and it has two handles so that you can easily carry it into the shower and hook it in place. The two handles serve as the hook. All you need to do is find someplace to attach it. With most showers, there is a single handle that controls the water and it’s usually pointed up, making it ideal for this purpose. You can hook it to the shower head also, provided it doesn’t slip off. It depends on the design of the shower head, of course.

This caddy has seven pockets which is more than enough to hold your shower essentials. The best feature is the mesh design. It allows it to drain so that you don’t unexpectedly find water still in your caddy later. The caddies that feature a solid plastic design often do not have a means to drain. You have to empty the caddy, turn it upside down, and let it drain and dry. This is accomplished with little to no effort with this caddy. And because the mesh is see- through, you know what you’re reaching for.

If you travel or if you’re student living in a dorm, a portable shower caddy can prove quite useful. This caddy from the Handy Laundry Store is a very good one for general use. It has more than enough compartments and it the mesh design helps it dry quickly. It makes a good back to college gift for students.
