Ubiquinol AKA CoQ10 AKA Coenzyme Q10 is possibly one of the most important nutraceuticals one could choose to take, and this particular version of it is from a reputable company, though not the only company I would consider using. Other possibilities include: [[ASIN:B004VCOOUU Jarrow Formulas]], [[ASIN:B003VBK5RS Life Extension]], and [[ASIN:B001PYZCZI Solgar]].

CoQ10 is a powerful antioxidant, and it is a critical player in all of the energy-production pathways in the human body. It is found in every cell, and its name, "ubiquinol," derives from it being "ubiquitous" in the body. Because it is associated with energy production, it is found in highest concentration in the organs with the greatest requirement for energy, namely the liver, kidneys and heart. CoQ10 is also an important element in immune function. Supplemental CoQ10 has been found to help the body fight off infection and tumors, and there are promising research findings using CoQ10 to treat HIV/AIDS.

Not surprisingly, because of these vital functions of CoQ10, research indicates it can help prevent or heal many diseases, including (among others): all types of heart disease (heart attack, angina, arrhythmia, atherosclerosis, congestive heart failure, mitral valve prolapse, and high blood pressure), cancer, diabetes, gum disease, muscular dystrophy, infertility, migraine headaches, and stomach ulcers. Research also indicates that CoQ10 can improve brain function.

A healthy, young human body can store the equivalent of 2 grams (2000 mg) of CoQ10, and 0.5 grams (500 mg) of that needs to be replaced daily through either food or a supplement such as this one. Dietary sources of CoQ10 include meat, poultry, fish, eggs, soybean, nuts, and canola oil. Fruits, vegetables, eggs, and dairy products contain modest amounts of CoQ10. By a process called "endogenous synthesis," the body can produce within it a fraction of the CoQ10 that it needs. However, beginning as early as age 21, endogenous synthesis already begins to decline. Though CoQ10 can be gained externally through the diet, most people don't get nearly enough that way. In developed nations of the West, the average CoQ10 in our diet is on average 5-10 mg/day--or only, at best, 1/50th of what we need to stay healthy. This means that even people who are not suffering from disease would be well advised to supplement CoQ10 in their diet.

Those who are taking statins to lower cholesterol particularly need to supplement CoQ10, because statins block whatever ability to perform endogenous synthesis of CoQ10 that remains in the body--which is very small by the age statins are typically prescribed, the forties and above. It is a tragic irony that though statins are prescribed to presumably reduce the risk of heart disease, they can actually result in heart disease, because they decrease CoQ10 levels in the body. Insufficient CoQ10 caused by statins can also lead to chronic fatigue, and it can contribute to or cause diabetes--a condition that many patients prescribed statins may already have due to obesity. In addition, all statins are known to cause, in varying degrees, the horrible condition of rhabdomyolysis. This is an extreme form of muscle cell breakdown that causes pain, disability and even death.

[[ASIN:034549802X Dr. Andrew Weil]] recommends a soft-gel ubiquinol such as this product, because it works better as an antioxidant than CoQ10 in the form of ubiquinone. Because CoQ10 is fat soluble, it should be taken with a meal containing fat.

Dr. Weil recommends that adults taking statins or those with a family history of heart disease take 90-120 mg. of supplemental CoQ10, which would be about two of these 50 mg. capsules. In contrast, a dosage for those who do not have either of those issues, but who want to prevent heart disease or take CQ10 as a powerful antioxidant, could be as little as 30-50 mg. of CoQ10 per day, or the equivalent of one of these 50 mg. capsules.

Given the amounts listed above that the body supposedly needs to be healthy, I was rather surprised that supplementing a mere 1/10th of the 500 mg. of CoQ10 what we need daily would be presumed to be an adequate dosage. I was particularly surprised that dosages much lower than that are recommended by Dr. Weil for patients taking statins, given that there have been studies where participants safely took up to 1200 mg. per day, in divided dosages. Perhaps the hesitation is because CoQ10 is very expensive. Whatever the reason, I am personally hopeful that for healthy people such as myself who are taking it for disease prevention, 50 mg./day truly is adequate, because that is the dosage that I take.

This is the core of my personal electronics repair and cleaning kit. It has all of the basic tools you will need to take apart most electronics that you dont need specialized equipment for.

Its a little pricey, but overall, its great quality. I have taken apart and repaired and/or cleaned quite a few things with it at this point. Everything from my old ASUS netbook for a repaste, a PS3 Slim for a cleaning, repaste, and repad, a PS4 Pro for cleaning, repasting, and repadding, are all straightforward to pull apart using the tools in this kit. I managed to save my broken PS3 by opening it up to solder the fan header, fix my Dualshock 4 controller with its sticky buttons, save my Pokemon Pinball cartridge from a leaky battery, clean and save my N64 rumble pack from battery acid, among the many things that this kit helped with. I will be using this kit for sure when it comes time to get into more higher risk electronics repair and maintenance, like when I crack open my GPU for a repaste and repad.

This is the kit that is at the center of getting things open so i can do what is needed with them. Get some other tools for cleaning, like ESD safe brushes, cans of compressed air, 99+% isopropal alcohol, and basic thermal management replacement items like some good thermal paste and pads, and you are good to go for general maintenance and cleaning. If you want to get into basic repairs, you will need a set of soldering tools and accessories, including a soldering iron, solder, wires, flux, solder wick, etc.

There are a couple missing things from this kit that would make it complete, one thing would be a ground plug. There is an ESD strap included, but you will need to find a place to clip it to. Having a ground plug would guarantee that you have somewhere to ground yourself to. Another thing would be a pair of micro pliers, as there are often cables plugged into sockets that are a pain to get out (I got a pair of Hakko long nose micro pliers with teeth and a taper to a 1.3mm nose). If you yank on the cable header incorrectly, there is a good chance that you will damage something. The pliers would help you properly grip those headers to pull them with the least chance of damaging things, tweezers are not strong enough to properly grip in those situations.

One note about my experience with this kit. I have not tried to pull apart anything that is specifically designed to deter repair (as an example, I dont own anything made by Apple). If you want to be able to open up and fix/clean/maintain your anti-repair item, you might want to buy a heat gun and IR thermometer on the side, along with replacement adhesive (you will be surprised at how much glue is used in something like a recent Macbook, and how ridiculously hard they make it to do simple things, like replacing a battery, or replacing/upgrading a hard-drive).

So if you want to switch from your phone to your computer, you need to explicitly disconnect from the phone, then connect from the computer. What can I say that hasn't been said by 6,200 previous buyers except that this Harmony 650 in silver is a great remote for a small single-remote system.

I'm using it on a patio with a TiVo, a Vizio 40" and an Amazon Basics SB20 sound bar. All three devices were easily found in the Harmony database and entered effortlessly into the remote using the MyHarmony app you download from Logitech to your laptop or desktop computer.

Having used the MyHarmony app to integrate my two Harmony Ultimate hubs for more complex remote IR systems that employ my network/router/phone as interfaces, I was already familiar with how Logitech has set up their software -- so it took only minutes to get the 650 into action.

Hint: before beginning to program your remote, gather the manufacturer and exact model number for each device you are going to control: TV, Amp, Sound Bar, Cable box, DVD player, Blu-ray Player, CD player, whatever. The MyHarmony software will ask you to add all the devices you are going to integrate. You'll need information from as many devices as you have current remotes for. When you're done, you put all the remotes away and use just the 650.

According to the MyHarmony app, the 650 can control 8 devices. I only needed to control three for my patio setup, so it was a simple process.

Bottom line, it's WAY easier to use a single Harmony 650 that to juggle three remotes (TiVo, Sound Bar and TV).

And after just a few minutes of easy online programming that then downloads to the 650 via a USB cable, I'm done.

As the 650 is being used on the patio outdoors, and subject to environmental attack from dust and moisture, I ordered the silicone cover for it. Works great: [[ASIN:B01N2SF2XX Harmony 650 Silicone Case for Logitech Harmony 650 700 Remote Controller Cover Anti Dust Anti-Slip]]

This BB cream took some experimentation to learn all its ins and outs. At first I wasn't sure I was going to like it, I kept trying to use it on top of my moisturizer because it just didn't feel like it was providing enough on its own. Given that it's water based, that went very very poorly. So I spent a week playing with it each day, trying different application techniques, layering options, and so on. This bad boy is so flexible, how you prep your skin, how you apply it, and how thickly you apply it, will completely change the result.

For me the first step in application for best results was having a very clean face. I suspect this product formula is highly non-ionic as it doesn't play well with oil or water, even though it's "water based". Any oil residue on my skin prevented it from going on smoothly and cleanly, and created "films" of white where the product set on top of skin oils and created odd textures and lines. Secondly, I also found that even though this product is supposed to be water based any water residue from cleansing would disrupt application as well. So clean air dried skin would be my first recommended step before trying this product.

The big three worth mentioning:

Super Dew finish:
Use your finger tip, apply in very tiny amounts and use dot motions to blend into your skin without rubbing. Yes, time consuming. But the outcome is lovely and unique, particularly for older women trying to recover that youthful dewy glowing skin look.

Powder finish:
Don't be shy with application, use finger tips to rub in thoroughly, the more you apply at once and the more you blend it in, the more of a powder finish you'll be left with. When done lightly blot with tissue. This works well when planning on applying other makeup products too.

Sheer color, Light Dew Finish:
Less is more for this one, but speed of application and minimal blending is important to keep the dew finish. Apply to skin, fingertips or beauty sponge work here, using very light motions blend across face, be careful not to rub it into the skin too much, let it absorb into the skin and set on its own.

All three of these application methods result in a very dynamic color, with the powder method being slightly more uniform deeper color coverage. It also responds well, and uniquely, to different finishing sprays. I use pure rose water, MAC fix it and forget it, or elf mist and set, all three work well, all three give a different finish.

Finally as to color, I have ridiculously fair transparent skin, bordering on a "pool" tone, that blue green water color. This BB cream is the ONLY BB cream I've ever used that was able to match my skin tone and provide some nice rose highlights so I don't look like the walking dead without having to use any other makeup products to add color. I've spent countless hundreds of dollars trying out every BB cream I could get my hands on, so when I say it's the only one, I mean it's the only one.

If you buy this and you can't get it to work with your skin tone, I'd suggest playing with application method before you give up on it. It really does alter the result. For instance I found I can't use a brush application method, it goes on too thick creating a flat color across my whole face and provides no moisture transference (it's like the brush broke all the water beads and evaporated them during application, and I was left with pure color).

It's such a lovely product, I can't recommend it enough. That doesn't mean it's for everyone, but it just might be for you.

I purchased this to use with a Kindle Fire HD 8.9 that I use as a dedicated music player, as I manage all of my music through Amazon Music. I have my Kindle tablet mounted on a wall, and I wanted a 90 degree micro USB cable to keep the cord neatly arranged. I had been using a standard micro USB cable until I could get a 90 degree one. It had been working fine, often with me leaving the player running all night.

After I received this cable and had been using it for some hours (estimate between 4-6 hours) my music shut off unexpectedly. When I checked on the problem I discovered my Kindle had shut down because the battery was exhausted even though it was plugged into USB through this cable the entire time. This cable is not allowing the Kindle to receive enough power through the USB port to keep the battery charged.

For the next 5 -10 minutes I tried turning my Kindle Fire tablet back on with this cable still plugged in, but all that would come on the screen was the low battery symbol. I then plugged back in my original USB cable and my Kindle tablet came back on. This revealed that this 90 degree cable is restricting the power (I had it plugged into a 2 amp USB charging port).

I have not been able to find another 90 degree micro USB cable where users are nor reporting similar problems, so I ordered the [[ASIN:B001EJHH20 Motorola Micro USB SKN6258 Adapter for RAZR2 V8 Q9m V9]] as a user reported testing the power throughput of the adapter without any noticeable loss. I will update this review after I test out the adapter to note whether it solves this problem.

October 4, 2015 Update:

Upon receiving the Motorola MICRO USB Adapter mentioned above, I found that my charging issues were immediately resolved. My Kindle charges quickly, and after a couple months of use it has never experienced battery drain. This proves that the Play X Store 90 Degree Micro USB Cable is restricting the amount of electrical current delivered through it and is an inadequate choice for the Kindle Fire.

I've had WD drives for decades, and the only issues I ever had were with WD Green and Black drives. Red, Red Plus, and Red Pro work where they're intended to work, as they're intended to work. So do WD Blue. Before buying a WD drive, learn what each color is intended for. The Black drives I've had fail were due to insufficient cooling. Blue are to be used in a PC with one or two drives that sees daily use. That's daily, not 24/365. Not in an array. Each level of Red drive is intended for arrays of different numbers of drives. They are not quiet desktop drives. You really want them somewhere other than next to where you sit.

More importantly than all that, carefully check prices in several places. Don't pay the absurd prices that some people want after buying their stock at retail price. They'll go back down. WD will make more.

I decided to get the Colormunki after struggling for over a year to get my Canon Pro9000 printer to produce prints that were consistently accurate representations of my photos, as they looked on my monitor - I had a monitor calibrator, but that's only one part of what you need in color management. I had used generic profiles for the paper I was using in the past and did all thing things you are supposed to do with the color management settings to get things right, but still experienced highly inconsistent results. After much reading, I determined that getting custom profiles for my printer/paper combinations might be the way to go. The Colormunki allows you to profile your printer specifically for the paper you are using, in addition to calibrating your monitor.

The profiler controls are easily understood and engaged; in order to profile the printer you will need to use at least two sheets of whatever paper you are profiling, and you will need to profile for each type of paper you use - each paper gets its own custom profile - so there is some initial expenditure of ink and paper to get your profiles ready. But that's nothing compared to the ink and paper you would have wasted trying to get an acceptable print without a custom profile, so I don't see that as a disadvantage.

Things did not go smoothly at first though - you're supposed to use the Colormunki to scan a series of color patches and when I first printed out my color patches my printer was apparently low on magenta and did not properly print out the patches that had magenta in it. I was unaware of that, and as I attempted to scan the patches, the Colormunki would simply tell me the scan had failed and not offer any tips as to where to begin locating the point of failure. It wasn't until I used the online help and wandered in and out of several articles (their online article resource is not well-organized) that I finally stumbled on a sentence that pointed me in the right direction. Once over that hurdle, the profiling proceeded very quickly and very easily. I was then able to make more profiles without any hitches at all. But my review gets 4 stars instead of 5, as I believe the makers of Colormunki could have done a much better job in creating and organizing the help documentation. There needs to be more of an effort on their part to address the questions that might arise for a user that has no knowledge of the finer points of color profiling - their help documentation seems to gloss over a number of things, or assume that the user would already know them. Given that the product is marketed to the general consumer, this is potentially a serious misstep on their part.

I cannot speak for the projector profiler feature as I do not have a use for that and have not tested it.

In summary, I've seen a vast improvement in the color accuracy of my prints since using the Colormunki, but be aware that troubleshooting any problems with this product can lead to a lot of frustration if you don't already have the expertise that would help you know where to start looking.

I have purchased about 30 different power banks from various vendors. I have brought the 10,000 miliamp power bank about 4 years and now this one from EasyAcc. Other manufacturers state their banks are 5000, 10,000, 15,000, 20,000 and higher and most are not even close to the rated capacities. The units from Easyacc are what they are rated or very close.

That said the power banks come with almost nothing this one did come with two short cables for charging and a small few page manual. If you are buying the bank for cables and extra junk go someplace else. This bank is fairly rugged and light works well. I can run my ipad and phone off this battery for at least a day 24 hours. In a normal 24 hour period I charge my phone 3 times at 3200 mah and I charge my ipad once but use it usually for 4 to 5 hours but for my test I ran it 24 hours. So my ipad has a 10,000 mah battery. So for 24 hours I would use the full 20,000 Mah supply. This held true plus some, the battery had one light still on after 24 hours pretty good.

Another area of concern is how many charges can the bank take. The old 10,000 Mah unit stated that it should be good for 500 charges. I have had it for now 4 years with way over 500 charges and it is still going strong, I rather someone tell me that something was not going to last and it last much longer then they say to you it will last thousands of charges and it last 50.

Next is size and weight. It is about 1/2" longer than my note 4 and the same width, it is also about 1/2" thick. It is not light weighing about 1/2 lb. So if you are going to camp with this unit you might consider it's weight. The unit is not water resistant that I can see but it is fairly ruggedly built and can take some punishment, so if out in the rain put it in a ziplock.

Charging time, They say it takes 6 hours but they also state you need to plug it into a 4 amp charger or 2 - 2 amp chargers. Be warned most phone chargers are only 1 amp so using 2 of the one amp chargers will take you almost twice as long to charge but IPad, and Iphone chargers are for the most part 2 amp chargers and will charge the unit in roughly 6 hours.

How good does the unit hold a charge. Most of you all are aware batteries leak power. This unit has remained fully charged for 2 months which is the longest I let go before draining and recharging it. As most of you all are also aware batteries die if not used so I drain and fill my batteries usually once a month.

Everything said this is by far the best power bank I have used.

A note on price: this is the best price I found for this particular model. You'll see identical stands from many sellers on other marketplaces, too. Some are several hundred dollars more for what clearly appears to be the same stand. I researched this, and found this seller to have the best price.

===

One more note for any hardcore fish people out there noticing there are fish in the tank: "Two weeks, and your fish are already in there??"

The scent is spot-on and really captures the intoxicating aroma of freshly-brewed strong, dark, coffee. When you initially spray it, it has a strong odor of alcohol, but that fades quickly into just coffee. The scent is very pure -- no sugar, cream, vanilla, hazelnut or other overtones -- it's just coffee. I think the aroma is perfect, and would be perfect for layering with other Demeter scents, particularly woodsy scents or vanilla scents.

The reason I gave this four stars instead of five -- the fragrance does not last at all. Seriously, five minutes after I spray it about ten times, I'm ready for more. I've found that this is typical for Demeter -- most Demeter fragrances lack any lasting power. But that is part of their appeal -- as you can mix them and use them more liberally than more more traditional (and expensive) perfumes, and you can mix and match to create your own scents. And because of the quick fade, the aromas are never overwhelming or overpowering. If I spray this around my cuffs or collar, I can catch a whiff of the fragrance on occasion. It's a nice pick me up.

I would definitely try this fragrance again -- I might try the roll-on perfume oil version to see if it has a little more lasting power.

I bought three different colors (orange crush, purple passion, and mermaid blue). As of now I can only truly evaluate orange crush. About 1/2 hour later I washed my hair which is pretty much a no no. Only leaving it in 30 minutes then washing instead of rinsing? It took pretty well despite my horrible treatment of it. Color was what I expected.

Now onto the orange crush - I have short hair (pixie'ish short) so nothing fancy here color wise. When I want to change colors I just go for the roots and if it'll work I color over the remaining color, if not, ease into the new w/ each root touch up. In the case of orange crush my roots were freshly bleached and toned, mid hair had been purple (Splat brand) faded almost all the way, lower hair still a very bright pink (Special Effects). I covered it all.

I don't hate it, but I also think it's closer to red than orange (even on the bleached roots). Next time I will mix in yellow to get a more true orange (the kind I'd expect from "orange crush"). That's the bad. The good is I've used Manic Panic, Raw, Splat, and Special Effects before Sparks. All left my neck and pillow covered in dye (to varying degrees but still, all did). Heat of summer without AC sweating in my sleep so dye should have run... But none on my neck or pillow the next morning! Yay.

Cannot yet tell you how long it lasts in my hair, but early feeling is that this is my new dye. Will update if my feelings change.

Should be noted I used about 2/3 tube with my short hair. Longer hair will definitely require multiple tubes but given the price, could still work out better than some competitors price wise.

Many of us would like to use our computer in a certain room or area of the house, but it really is too expensive, or too difficult, or not practical to run Cat5/6 Cable to the location (drilling holes, going through walls, floors, ceilings, etc.). There are also those situations, because of building structure and/or materials that wireless tends to drop internet connections or is unable to supply a desired or required amount of bandwidth.

In my own case, a few years ago, I needed a solution to bring the Internet to the 3rd floor of a 140 year-old building, which had wiring (only two-prong) more than just a few decades old. From previous experience, I knew wireless would not work (at least work well). There was also little or no hope, in the near future, of running a CAT5/6 line for a hardwired connection.

A fair amount of research first led me to find the [[ASIN:B001J2ZSL4 Cisco-Linksys PLK300 PowerLine AV Ethernet Adapter Kit]] (made up of two Cisco-Linksys devices: PLE300 & PLS300 network adapters). I was a skeptic, but the reviews on Amazon.com and other sites convinced me to give it a try. Because of this product, I had Internet service the same day the product was delivered. The PLE300 plugs into your router or switch and an electrical receptacle. The PLS300 plugs in a wall receptacle where you want to use the network/Internet. The PLS300 is a four-port adapter (having 4 RJ-45 connectors), acting like a normal switch, giving Network/Internet access to 4 computers or any other network devices.

Since then, I have updated (actually added) several components to the network including this [[ASIN:B006OOKT3Y NETGEAR Powerline 200Mbps Nano Adapter - Starter Kit (XAVB2101)]]. One of the units in the set replaces the above Cisco-Linksys PLE300 router connection. The other unit is now connected to my computer, replacing the PLS300 (now used elsewhere). The network connection boasts of up to 200Mbps data rates as the Cisco did. There are others, like the [[ASIN:B007ILFFS6 NETGEAR Powerline Nano Adapter - Starter Kit (XAVB5101)]] that claim speeds up to 500 Mbps. I have used them both. I find them impressive! Plus, it's all Plug and Play!

Besides these Powerline adapters, I know of no other solution that provides Internet access to any part of a home or office so quickly and efficiently. The network is easily expandable by plugging additional single-port adapters into electrical outlets anywhere in the building controlled by the same electrical service. A network switch like [[ASIN:B0000BVYT3 NETGEAR GS105 ProSafe 5-Port Gigabit Ethernet Desktop Switch - 10/100/1000 Mbps]] can then be plugged into the adapter, as I am doing, to allow several devices access to the network/Internet. From a user's standpoint, you should experience Internet speeds comparable to what any cable or DSL service provides. These are fast enough to watch streaming HD video from Netflix or other services on internet-ready HD TVs. It's cleaner and easier than most other solutions.

Since initially buying my first Powerline adapters, there have been many companies that have have gotten into the "powerline" market. Cisco/Linksys, Netgear, and Monster are just a few. A little research and reviews can point to many accessories that are compatible and backwards compatible with the Homeplug AV technology standard used in these products. This also competes with products like the [[ASIN:B003VWY0VY Western Digital WD Livewire Powerline AV Network Kit]].

Context

I purchased a used pair of Audeze LCDi3 a few months ago, from a seller who repeated a common complaint about these headphones - they just didn't seem to fit his ears. I bought these in particular because I wanted high-quality, open-back IEMs. I wanted the open-back ones because I use these around the house and while working out, but wanted full situational awareness when doing so, I really don't like losing one of my primary senses. However, when I received them, I found that no matter what I did, or what ear cushions I used, they just didn't feel quite right. I needed both ear cushions and ear-hooks to make them work, and that was finicky, they still tended to fall out. So I decided - rather than spend hundreds of dollars on custom IEM cushions, I'd just make my own.

Process

The process is very simple. You have two containers, each with one half of the putty. You divide each into two parts, and use one part of each to make one ear cushion, making one cushion first, letting it cure, then making the second. You knead it together for about 90 seconds, then begin forming. It is very pliable at first, and it may even help to let it cure for a minute or two to make it easier to work with, but I was able to form it right after mixing. It sticks in the ear on its own, and I had a little extra left over from each ear, a ball about 4mm across. I allowed for a cure time, in the ear, of 20 minutes, and you can tell its about ready because the extra ball sets up nice and firm, and you can sort of feel the ear cushion "pull away" from the skin of the ear when it is setting up. When it stops doing so, you know its ready.

I purchased a total of four sets of Radians, in the peach/flesh tone, to ensure I had plenty of extras to experiment with. The first set I just molded to my ears to make sure I liked the feel of them. They are comfortable, a bit harder when cured than most custom earplugs. Not a big issue, but don't pack it into your ear ridges -too- much or it will be uncomfortable when cured. The second pair I perfected the fit - I filled not only the ear canal, but also the ridge above it, and some of the ridge "forward" of it (closer to the front of the body). I then tried to cut a cylindrical hole for the IEM stem using a 1/4" drill bit (same diameter as the stem), and this worked, but the resulting earbud wasn't very tight and the ear cushion looked pretty rough around the hole. For the third set, I filled some 1/4" heat shrink tubing with epoxy, then formed the earplug around that, ensuring I had a nice, clear shot to the ear canal and the hole was level and aligned. This worked very well, and I am still using the third set today.

Review

They are quite comfortable. I was worried they'd be hot, or awkward, or unpleasant due to their hardness, but they stay in place very well. They are easy to put in and remove, with a little technique. I can wear them for hours without their bothering me. I can exercise, even doing lifts, sit-ups, push-ups, and pull-ups - without them giving me trouble. Even though they are supporting both the LCDi3 and their bluetooth cable, and thus not an insignificant weight of materials, they are as comfortable as when I was just using them as earplugs.

That said, I cannot comment on their ability to block noise, as I do not use them for that purpose. Also, my first two attempts produced ear cushions that were uncomfortable because I didn't include enough of the forward ear ridge to help support them, and I packed it in a bit too tight. So if they do ache or put pressure on your ear for more than an initial couple hour acclimation period, you might want to try again.

My only real complaint is that they aren't offered in black.

All in all, would recommend for use as custom ear cushions.

The installation process is tricky because of the liquid glue process. And it can be messy. This is important for best results:
take your time and read the instructions before starting. Pay close attention to the alignment of the screen protector in relation to the phone and installation tray.

Be sure to cure the glue with the UV light as in the directions. I rushed because I panicked thinking the glue would be hard to clean once it dried. If I could do it again, I would wipe just the uncured (liquidy) glue first, use the UV light to cure all the glue under the glass, then use Goo Gone and alcohol (in that order) to clean the rest.

This kit may seem pricey but if you consider the end results (great screen functionality) and the fact that you just paid for a nail polish curing UV light, it's worth more than the price.

this is a single-band antenna. That's in the description, but it bears repeating. It only receives UHF well.

Many tv stations are broadcasted at UHF, the higher frequency band, but there's still some in VHF, which is lower in frequency (similar frequency range as FM radio.)

Assembly was straightforward, just take your time and stay away from power tools to avoid damaging the particleboard. It took two of us about an hour and a half from opening the box to hanging the clothes and filling the very smooth sliding drawer. The interior shelf can be excluded if your clothes need extra length, but we are using it in ours. There are ballast boards on the bottom of the piece and they really do help keep this from tipping or becoming top heavy. All in all, we are satisfied, just hope it holds up longer than the warranty. It needs to be applied on the scalp. Even so, I can apply quite a bit near my temples where there is hair but clearly not much of it, and can rub it all in haphazardly, and my hair does not look wet or greasy.

A simple uncomplicated design and easy to assemble, and adjust.... with one problem.
Are you familiar with how 'C' clamps are made? They have a handle on the stem that allows the handle to be shunted back and forth. This allows close clamping where the handle won't get in the way of a vertical surface as you are winding it. This clamp doesn't have that. It has a hard right turn on the screwing post, and it has to sit farther away from the edge. This means that if you have a solid back desk, you will need a good 2" lip on the back of your desk to use this, or you will have to jury rig it like I did.
I took a small sturdy board and used a separate 'C' clamp to attach it to the desk, then clamped the monitor stand to that. It is back in a corner, so it doesn't show or interfere, but I thought you should be warned about this. Other than that, this is a strong and well made stand that would easily hold a bigger monitor than my 20" for sure.
The maximum clamping height is about 17 1/2" to the middle of the screen, and the maximum reach from the clamp post to the back of the screen is a little more than 9". That puts my screen front at aprox 11 1/2" out from the post.
All in all, except for that little problem that I would have apprecisted a head-up on, it is a great stand.

I was researching televisions for MONTHS and could not figure out which one to buy. My boyfriend is better at this stuff, so after I spent countless hours comparing TVs in Target, Wal-Mart and PC Richards, (and even securing a pre-order for a Coby, [which I quickly cancelled after hearing bad things]), I told him to see what he could find on Amazon. He found this TV and after sorting out what could be "insider reviews" from genuine ones, we decided that it sounded like a great deal for the money, and though the name is not exactly a household one yet, it was worth a shot, as another buyer said the same thing happened with Vizio a couple of years back.

So, we bought it for each other as a joint Christmas gift, figuring what the hey. If it wasn't as advertised, we'd send it back. And it had a lot to live up to, considering this was essentially our only gift to each other this year. It has been over a month now, and we LOVE this television.

Pros:

- No side glare - you can see the picture well, even if you are sitting on the side of the television.
- It is lightweight and super thin, so it is easy to transport.
- Very clear picture.
- Decent enough sound - you don't really need a sound bar if you don't have one, especially since there are options to change the sound (i.e. "music", "film", "surround sound", etc.)
-Provided you are not signed in to a game system (which you can change the video input from your remote), there is a setting where the TV will automatically shut itself off after 10 minutes of lack of use. This is very helpful if you have a roommate who tends to fall asleep in front of the television.
- There are plenty of settings to customize the picture and sound, as well as "label" your game systems with the pre-loaded options so you know which video input to select for your X-Box or PS3 (for example, I have the PS3 set to "Blue Ray", whereas the X-Box is set to "Game").

Cons:

-It is not a "smart TV", if you are in the market for one of those. It's a simple design, which was perfect for us.
-There are no buttons on the TV itself, so if the remote ever breaks, I have no idea how we are going to turn it on and off, aside from buying a new remote.
-There are a shortage of plugs in the back for cables. For example, I can hook up the cable box, X-Box and PS3, but there is no room now for the sound bar. Not a huge deal, but I could see where some people might find that to be annoying.

This television lived up to all of the positive reviews it received here on Amazon, and I am so thoroughly satisfied that we decided to go with this one that I kept reminding myself to write this review so I could help others who were as in the dark as we were about which TV to buy. I didn't get the dreaded "green screen" upon turning it on, as some people have experienced, and the packaging didn't overly give it away that it was a TV, (though we got the 48" one, so I'm sure people could figure it out).

Bottom line: If you are in as much doubt as we were about which TV to buy, trust us on this one - TCL rocks!

This lens pen is just what I need in a compact, easy-to-carry product. I am a photographer who has to carry a lot of gear outside. Having something compact and light is essential.

One side is a brush to get rid of fine and large particles of material from the lens. The other side is to remove oils (e.g. fingerprints) and is made of a fine material that has a carbon dust cleaning solution embedded in it.

The first three to five uses can be a bit frustrating as this carbon dust is quite heavy and will actually leave a slight residue on the lens. In this case I just used the brush first, the carbon cleaner second, and then finished up with the brush again to remove any extra carbon. I had no artifacts in my photos at all. After the initial break-in period this lens pen performs flawlessly.

The pen is close to 4 inches long (without the brush extended) and about 3/4 inches wide. Its actually very compact and light. It has a tab on the cap to be able to secure it while its in a pocket, just like a regular pen. The brush is about an inch long and is used by extending it out of the end of the pen. It adds about an inch of length when extended. The carbon cleaner is covered by a cap which is screwed off in order to expose the cleaning surface. I wish there was a spot to put this cap while using the carbon cleaning side. Its the only long term con to this pen.

Pros:
*Light
*Compact
*Cleans lenses well
*Easy to carry in pocket
*Cheap

Cons:
*Carbon dust residue for first 3-5 uses.(-1/4 star)
*Cap has no place to be put on the pen while using it. (-1/4 star)

This device isn't for everyone, but it fits my needs perfectly. Here is how I use it - during meetings I take notes, do sketches (user interfaces, high-level system design diagrams, etc.), and list follow-up items. This material is automatically beamed to my Palm Vx as pictures of the sketches and/or notes. I upload these to my PC and email them as attachments. This gets information out quickly, which can be followed up later with more refined notes transcribed into a word processor (by hand) or better drawings (I use Visio).
It does one thing only - captures pictures of what you write on plain paper - and it does that exceptionally well.

If your needs are similar to mine stated above and you have either a Palm or Pocket PC PDA you will probably love this notepad. JARROW FORMULAS SACCHAROMYCES BOULARDII + MOS (180 Veggie Capsules) is a probiotic. Saccharomyces Boulardii is useful for preventing and treating diarrhea (e.g., traveler’s diarrhea), as well as for promoting general intestinal health, and for treating irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), inflammatory bowel disease (IBD, Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis), Lyme disease, and other bowel disorders.

Mannanoligosaccharides (MOS) are nondigestible chains of the sugar mannose, which act as decoys to unfriendly bacteria in the digestive tract. “Bad” microorganisms seeking a long-term foothold in the intestines may bind with the MOS, and get a ride through and out of the system instead.

OF SPECIAL NOTE: Saccharomyces boulardii is yeast (fungus), so it interacts with anti-fungal medications. It's generally safe for adults, but may be dangerous for children or for people with compromised immune systems. It causes gas in some people. The dosage is 1-2 capsules per day. The capsules contain no wheat, no gluten, no soybeans, no dairy, no egg, no fish/shellfish, no peanuts/tree nuts.

This probiotic seems to have no ill effects on me (maybe some extra gas). It seems to help with my IBS (as all probiotics do). My experience with Jarrow products has always been good--it’s a brand that I trust to contain the ingredients the label says the product contains, and to do more or less what the label says the product will do.

My points of comparison are a Galaxy Tab S6 Lite 10.4-inch Android Tablet 128GB that I purchased in June 2021, and my first large format Galaxy, the Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro SM-T9000ZWAXAR 12.2-Inch Tablet that I purchased in June 2015.

This one is a major performance improvement over the most recent (June 2021) Galaxy, and better in all respects than the much older 12.2 Galaxy I purchased in June 2015.

I was totally pleased with the Tab S6, but missed the larger screen of the Tab Pro 12.2. This screen is significantly more vivid than the 12.2 Tab Pro, and the 256gb memory in this one pretty much assures that the performance is significantly better than either the 32GB Tab Pro or the 128GB Tab S6. But that is expected.

What I truly love about this tablet over the older large format one is the body is sturdy and not prone to bending. That is why my Tab Pro ultimately failed: the body was so thin that it flexed and at some point it started acting crazy. It would have cost more to repair it than to purchase the Tab S6. Prior to purchasing this one I made sure that that issue had been resolved. Yes, it's not as light, but it more than makes up for it in sheer speed, superior display, and even sound quality.

If you want or need a large format tablet that is reasonably priced and provides excellent battery life and performance this is worth considering.

I tried a different wrist splint and a hot/cold wrap before I found this splint. If you developed Jose DeQuervo Tennis Center Ivy like I did, you may have noticed most all of them have a design flaw---they put pressure on the sore spot, the area of the wrist directly below and in line with the thumb. That's where the sore tendons and collar are. So you can wake up with more soreness than you went to bed with.

This one I like better because I was able to modify it to bridge over that part of the wrist while keeping my thumb and hand stabilized to cut down on lateral pivoting movement. I made a cut in the sleeve that holds the plastic thumb splint (not one of the two aluminum ones), removed the splint, and replaced it with one I made by beating flat a length of 1/4-inch copper tubing. I filed the ends smooth and rounded them slightly. I annealed it (made it bendable) by heating it with a propane torch and letting it cool.

I was then able to shape that splint to bridge over my sore wrist. I also shaped the two aluminum splints to suit. I leave the middle strap very loose, so it doesn't tighten down on the wrist area. I just tighten the upper and lower straps and the thumb strap. When I say tighten, I don't mean tight tight. I mean just enough to be secure and stabilize things.

So anyway this wasn't ideal out of the box, but it was better than others I looked at because I was able to modify it to make it work better for me.

I needed to replace my aging WD NAS, which was struggling to keep up with my needs. After quite a bit of research and product comparisons, I decided to go with the market leader, and bought a NAS that seemed likely to be able to support my needs for several years, and offered some options for expanding the ways I use a NAS.

For context, I mainly use my NAS as "network-attached storage": I back up files, and I share files for use on our multiple home computers. I don't use it for remote access (security concern: I'd rather use cloud storage services for that), and I don't use it as a repository for a media server, or anything else like that.

I decided to use WD "Red" drives for this unit: based on specs and user and professional reviews, they seemed most likely to run reliably for as long as I needed. My previous experience with WD black, blue, and red drives has been consistently positive, whereas other vendors have let me down.

Installation and setup was very easy: I had the unit up and running within a few minutes. Copying files over from my old NAS took some time, but the performance of this Synology unit exceeded my expectations. I was also pleased with how much faster my backup jobs were. I was especially pleased when apps that use network files began running much faster: so clearly both read and write performance were much improved in comparion with the old system.

I also set up a USB backup. It took a little bit of reading in the Synology KB to learn how to do it right, but after that it was a breeze. I plugged in a USB hard drive in the back port (the front port can be configured for use with the USB Copy button), opened up the Hyper Backup app, and ran the initial backup to copy the entire NAS contents to the USB drive. Then I scheduled it to run incremental jobs every day, so now my paranoid backup demon is happy. (I save backup drives in a secure location to provide "disaster recovery"; overkill perhaps, but it buys peace of mind.)

One criticism: the unit came with only 2GB memory, which seems cheesy. And what makes is super-cheesy is the way they price their branded "compatible memory" at ridiculous multiples of the market price. I was able to buy a 4GB Samsung memory card for under $15, and it worked just fine. You can do a web search and see that others have upgraded using larger memory cards.

The Synology KB website is very good: it's well written and comprehensive. There's also an active user community, so there is a ton of information easily available. Overall I'm very happy with my Synology purchase, and would buy their NAS products again without hesitation.

The Reveal kit also comes with three microfiber cleaning pads which cling tenaciously to the mop head, and do a damn good job of soaking up the solution. Peel them off, rinse them out or toss them in the washing machine, and reuse. No more waste!

Another plus is the Reveal doesn't need batteries for the spray function. The Swiffer required 4 AA batteries, and while the power use was minimal, I really don't see why it was necessary when Rubbermaid has done the same thing mechanically. However that brings me to my one criticism of the Reveal: The spray is rather high. If you are too close to a cabinet or wall, or a piece of furniture when you pull the trigger, quite a lot of your solution will end up on the cabinet, wall, etc. Spray well back from where you want to be mopping.

The Reveal is heavier than the Wet Jet, but not by much. It's easy to maneuver and moves quite smoothly, better in fact than the Wet Jet, which flipped around a bit. It doesn't have an abrasive pad, but anyone who ever tried to use the one on the Wet Jet will probably tell you that it wasn't much better than none at all. I don't really miss it. If there's something I need to scrub, I can spot clean.

I know Rubbermaid quality and I'm guessing this won't fall apart as quickly as my first Wet Jet did. Seriously, all things considered, I don't think you could ask for too much better than this unit. Sorry Swiffer.

I bought a refurbished remote from amazon a few weeks ago. It has been working like a champ. There is nothing more enjoyable than having one button setup your entire theater system based on an activity. Finally my wife/kids or the babysitter can setup everything to watch a movie or play a game without calling me to ask what to do next.

There have been no issues with it, and even the connectors on the remote to the charger are fine. I've never had to mess around with it to get the connection to work. Just drop it on the charger and off it goes.

It's best when your devices use discreet codes to control the device. Otherwise the remote tries to switch the input by going through the menu and adjusting it as though you were pushing the buttons. This isn't bad if it works. For my setup, my AV Receiver doesn't work with discreet codes so it tries to adjust the optical input by remembering where it was before and adjusting accordingly. Most of the time it gets it wrong and I have to use the help button to correct it.

The help button is a life saver also. If something doesn't work the wizard will send out all the codes again, and ask you if it fixed it, if it didn't then it will go through a process of asking if things are on and on the right input and try to fix it. This is great for the wife or kids also.

The software that is used doesn't run all the time as another person suggested. At least version 7.3 doesn't. It only runs when I run it.

It take a bit of time and patience to work through the programming to get it all setup for your system, but it's mostly just tweaking delays, etc as the Harmony/Logitech device database is immense and has most of the common devices already to setup in the remote.

Setting up the activities are a breeze. You just tell it which devices to use, which inputs to use, and what you want to control the volume, etc. It's great as I use my 5.1 system for DVD's and 360 so I want the AV Receiver to control the volume for those, but for the Wii and a VCR tape, I want the volume control to be on the TV. This remote can do both. It switches the volume control based on the activity. Simply Brilliant.

Overall, I highly recommend this remote. Even though it is refurbished, since it comes with the same year warranty that the new one comes with, you can't go wrong. I've bought two refurbished and both work great. Both look brand new. I can't see anything on them to suggest that they were once used other than the white box it comes in.

I have used these when I have gone beyond the basic limits of the [[ASIN:B004YAYM06 NETGEAR N300 Wi-Fi Range Extender - Wall Plug Version (WN3000RP)]]. They are very easy to configure. You simply plug these into your router or a switch and they have their own "Genie" and either wizard or manual "Setup" to choose from. It's pretty much self-explanatory. Basically, you have to tell it the name of the "Wireless Network Connection" you want it to pick up from. You then have to give a name to your extender, or let it generate one by adding on "_EXT" to your "Wireless Network Connection" name. It can also work hardwired to the router or a switch. These devices and their "Genies" can also be accessed by IP Address. It makes it really easy to work with. These can also be easily daisy-chained off of each other to produce some incredible long-rage effects. You can setup a second one to pick up its wireless signal from the first one, and so forth. There is a limit, however, to how far each of these can work, i.e. the distance that can be between two of these, or one of these and another wireless device. Should you find that you have reached that limit, don't give up hope. Look into a pair of [[ASIN:B0049AVWAO Ubiquiti NSM5 NanoStation M5]] devices. You can hook these up in a transparent manner so that they work like a long CAT5 cable (even though they are 802.11n, 5GHz wireless radios). That's what I did and then hooked one of these Netgear WN2000RPTs on the other end. It let me extend the network ½ block, way beyond what these Netgear WN2000RPTs are capable of doing. You can also use a NanoStation M5 to create a "HOTSPOT." You can buy a 802.11n, 2.4GHz version of the NanoStation M5 or a 2.4GHz version of the [[ASIN:B004EHSV4W Ubiquiti NanoStation loco M5]] that is more universally compatible for that use, or a [[ASIN:B005H4CDF4 Ubiquiti UniFi Long Range Access Point, (2.4 GHz, UAP-LR-US, US Version)]]. I do not think they will disappoint you.

I found that these refurbished units are usually cheaper than the [[ASIN:B004YAYM06 NETGEAR N300 Wi-Fi Range Extender - Wall Plug Version (WN3000RP)]]. They also have 4 Ethernet ports that can extend your CAT5 wired world. At current prices, as I write this, you could buy two or three of these for the price of one of those and produce a greater effect in extending your wireless network.

This is a great, high quality multi-featured amp that's very impressive at this price point. I'm writing this review after using it for about a week so I could get a feel for it and let my ears adjust.

I ordered the T4 to drive a pair of PSB Alpha 3 speakers rated at 8 ohms and with a recommended amp power off 10-80 watts. Other components are a Schiit modi DAC, with the audio source as hi-res files coming from an iMac. I would describe the sound quality as precise, with a slightly warm color, as you would expect and want when using tubes. The amp drives the speakers quite capably for near field listening. On albums mastered at lower levels (some classical music) I had to set the volume fairly high but overall it was more than enough for my speakers. I also own the Aiyima A07 amp, which is rated 300Wx2. The power difference between the two is noticable, as you'd expect, and the A07 sound profile is cooler. I also feel like the soundstage sounds a bit more layered with the T4 than with the A07.

Setup was a breeze with the included power supply; I was up and running in 5-10 minutes. The bluetooth antenna is a great bonus feature, rarely seen on a tube amp in this price range and the audio quality was great streaming from my iPhone. No connection issues while walking around a 1BR apartment. It's nice to be able to toggle to bluetooth and let guests stream from their phone directly to your system.

The included tubes are high quality and I appreciate the possibility of trying out a range of different tubes in the future. One thing to keep in mind for those new to audio gear is that you probably won't want to leave this or any tube amp always on, since all tube amps get warm and there will be wear on the tubes. That said, even good tubes are relatively inexpensive, so not a huge concern.

Last but not least it looks great! I personally like the vintage tube aesthetic, and this piece of kit has a lot more character than the usual drab black box. Since I don't have a ton of space, I much prefer these smaller amps over a huge black box receiver. The build quality is really solid -- glad to have this latest addition in the mix.

In full disclosure, I must admit that I miss my Bose Bluetooth speaker. Their acoustics are impeccable. The "Tribit XSound Go Bluetooth Speakers" only cost a fraction of my Bose speaker. I first purchased the "DOSS Touch Wireless Bluetooth" which is in the same price range; I returned that product because it lacked bass and was unimpressive overall. The Tribit, however, has plenty of bass for such a small speaker. Ironically, the problem that I have is the treble! I think it is an inherent problem with smaller speakers and not this particular device. I have installed an equalizer on my computer which mitigates some of the problems and makes the speaker sound very acceptable.

The pros:
• The speaker is loud! It is perfect for a jam session in your bedroom. I'm not sure it is suitable for large or multi rooms.
• The quality is good, and the speaker looks like a million bucks.
• It has an excellent microphone that works well with phone calls and even to interact with Siri or Cortana.
• The Play button allows one to answer, reject or end a call. It also can play or pause a song. Finally, it allows you to skip a music track forward or backward.

The cons:
• While the bass is fairly impressive, the treble is slightly overriding.
• The battery does not nearly last for 24 hours if you like to blast music as I do
• The speaker can only be paired to one device at a time. If you are listening to music on the computer and the phone tries to connect, the speaker will sometimes disconnect from all devices. The speaker does have an av input one could connect to the computer but obviously, the speaker would no longer be completely portable. This could be a deal breaker for many.

After comparing this speaker with others in its price range, I realize that this speaker has such poor sound quality that I could never recommend it to anyone.

The Onkyo HT-S5100 Home Entertainment System sounded quite good when listening to the radio, and I really loved the self-calibration feature to set the speaker phase/power-level based upon our optimum seating position.

When the receiver is played at low to mid volume ranges, the system was impressive, but there was distoration at higher levels when the speakers were driven beyond their capabilities.

As far as a Stereo Receiver goes, I'd give it high marks, but as far as a Home Entertainment system goes... in my opinion, I'd purchase something else.

I found after many frustrating hours of trying to get the receiver to work with my other HDMI components, that all of my attempts were in vain.

I'd essentially purchased the system on the recommedation of Consumer Reports (They crowed about the HT-S5100 having the best sound of any system they'd ever tested, and it was one of the only ones offering 7.1 versus 5.1 stereo surround).

I eventually re-read the Onkyo Owners Manual and found a small blurb regarding the audio of the system not working with HDMI...

I freely admit I'd blown-off the fact that analog/digital connectors were shown on the Quick Hook-Up illustrations (thinking these were alternative connections for those unlucky soul's who didn't have HDMI), when I finally resorted to contacting Onkyo for assistance/confirmation.

They confirmed my worst-fear, their HDMI's were (Pass-Though). When asked why they even bothered to put HDMI connectors on the system, the reply was (some consumers desired them).

Personally, I feel if a system has HDMI connectors present, that is implies they're fully compliant, otherwise their presence is misleading.

What this meant was all of my new toy's (50" Plasma, Blu-ray player, and Xbox 360) could only pass on video (not the higher quality audio signals through the HDMI connectors), and that I'd have to accept a lower quality audio output due to the use of standard audio connectors.

Perhaps I'd missed this in CR's review (or it wasn't stated), as I had to purchase additional digital cabling so that I could even hear the audio content of the devices hooked into the Onkyo (added expense/wiring woe's).

If I had to do it all over again, I'd purchase the HT-S5100 as a Stereo Receiver, but I wouldn't recommend it as the hub for a Home Entertainment System to interconnect your HDMI devices.

Microingredients offers substantial milligrams of an Omega-3 Fish Oil. The total Omega-3 Fatty Acid is 3,750mg, EPA at 2,000mg, DHA at 1,500 & what they call “other fatty acids” at 250mg. The standard milligram that is recommended is 1,000mg with 5,000mg being safe. I purchased this as it was on sale & the # of soft gels being 300 was attracting so I swayed from my usual brand Sports Research which has 1,250mg of Omega-3 Fish Oil. This was an impulsive buy & I’m glad it wasn’t a costly one because this brand isn’t for me. Yes, it offers very high milligrams in all the categories that fall under an omega-3 fish oil but what I didn’t know until I received the bag was that 3 soft gels were recommended daily. Now these soft gels are ONE INCH in length. I personally do not have trouble swallowing pills & can swallow one at a time. This may be an issue for some to swallow just one. My thoughts in seeing the high milligrams prompted me to talk to my Doctor on how much I truly needed. I’m a healthy 52yo female. He informed me that the standard 1,000mg is well enough. He said the higher milligrams would be more needed for people with cardiac issues & other medical issues in which their doctor would advise them to take a higher dose. I didn’t take these for very long & went back to my normal brand. I’m not saying this is a bad brand of omega-3 fish oil. I feel it’s best to consult with your doctor to see if you truly need to consume this much. Also note there is a bit of a fishy aftertaste.

I've had this processor running in my new build for about a month now. I was being annoyed by the stock cooler fan buzzing at very high rpm whenever the heat rose to moderate levels like 52C. I cleaned the cooler base and the CPU thoroughly and applied a pea sized spot of Arctic Silver 5 then reassembled everything.
Instant cure. Instant quieter fan. Instant low CPU temps andQUIET!AMD needs to stop using whatever they're putting on the coolers and just include a syringe of a high quality thermal paste for customers to apply themselves because whatever they're using is junk.
The stock cooler and fan they include with the fx 8320 are very high quality but the pre applied thermal paste is garbage.
Just apply new first quality thermal paste, you don't need to spend big dollars on third party hardware and I suspect those of you who have installed new coolers and seen great results is because of the new thermal paste used during installation.
The fx 8320 is a very powerful processor don't smoke it because of 10 cents worth of cheap thermal paste, use the best for your investment and this hot CPU will give many years of great performance.

This trolley is ideal for augmenting buffets as well as providing extra storage and display space in cramped quarters. I have uploaded five customer-supplied photos at the top of this page to depict the relative size as well as some construction details.

Assembly would have been a snap had it not been for two very minor issues that slowed me down. The first was a deformed screw head for one of the drawer glides that I had to insert with pliers instead of a phillips screwdriver. In fact, all you need to assemble this is a phillips screwdriver - the other tool for the larger screws ships with the trolley. The second issue was the drawer handle had to be slightly bent to align with the holes in the face of the drawer. Minor to me, but could prove frustrating to someone who has never or rarely assembled furniture.

The instructions are highly visual. I have uploaded a photo of them at the top of this page. They are in a storyboard format that may be confusing to some folks. I ignored them because having assembled a lot of pre-fabricated furniture this was a simple task. Bless the learning curve.

All of the parts mate and the drawer effortlessly slides. The bamboo is an attractive material that is sturdy and resistant to moisture. However, I did mention that this is a no frills trolley. If you check the photos I supplied at the top of this page you will see that viewed from the side the drawer is not completely enclosed. Thus it will collect dust inside. Also, the screws used to fasten the major components are not countersunk, nor are wood plugs provided to cover them. If you are looking for aesthetics as well as function you will be disappointed.

Function is why I purchased this and why I love it. First, it takes up very little space. Second, it's a convenient refreshment station at a wine and cheese party or similar social gathering, as well as a display and storage piece for everyday use.

Do note that the wine rack on this is almost an afterthought. It will comfortably hold most 750ml bottles (unless the bottle is odd-shaped), and will even support three smaller 375ml bottles. It will NOT work with anything larger than 750ml though.

Aside from the minor assembly glitches this is a wonderful product for no frills, compact storage or serving. I love mine so much that I am pondering the purchase of a second unit.

This CEREALMATE NONSOGGY CEREAL BOWL is perfect for eating [[ASIN:B003XFOXQ6 Weetabix]], which is currently my favorite breakfast cereal. Weetabix soaks up milk in the blink of an eye, so I avoid soggy biscuits by dropping them into the milk and dragging them right back up onto the platform, one by one. If a biscuit doesn't get enough milk, I just dunk it again. The fact that the bowl doesn't have a barrier lip or ridge makes it easy to move the biscuits in and out of the milk.

The bowl is 8-1/2" across, divided into a 5"-wide platform for cereal and a 3-1/2"-wide reservoir for milk. The platform is large enough for an adult-size serving of any biscuit-type dry cereal (e.g., Weetabix, shredded wheat). The reservoir holds about 7 oz. of milk (just over 3/4 cup).

You can use this bowl for dry cereal other than biscuit-type cereal (e.g., Cheerios, mini-wheats, cornflakes), but the cereal will tend to slide into the reservoir. For those kinds of cereal, a bowl with a low barrier that holds the dry cereal in place will probably work better (e.g., [[ASIN:B00EDQCOX8 NEW Anti-Soggy Cereal Bowl]], [[ASIN:B00A2L1Q78 Obol Never-Soggy Cereal Bowl]]).

This is an excellent value and a great choice for someone looking for an inexpensive set of trimmers of reasonable quality.

I am not an expert on trimmers and I'll admit that up-front. My requirements were mainly value-based and my goal was to get a product that is of higher quality than a generic brand, while still staying inexpensive. When I got these, the kit was $21, which is certainly inexpensive and actually LESS than many of the no-name generic kits. I bought these for basic things like trimming my beard, maintaining neck line, touchups, side burns, etc. For this usage they have worked really well for me. I use the corded trimmer maybe once a week, and the battery-powered trimmer a few times a week. Three years after purchase, both products work as well as they did when they were new.

These are not built to a quality standard that professional Wahl products are (and they are not priced that way either.) They are built for and marketed as a value home-use product, and I think they do a very good job at this role. After three years, my own usage has found that the...
---blades themselves have remained sharp,
---guards work well to prevent cuts,
---battery life on the trimmer is excellent, and
---overall construction is very solid considering the price.
---Also, the included carry kit, guards, oil, and brush are also a nice addition as they avoid having to spend more money down the road and they give me everything I need in a single and inexpensive kit.

If your needs are for professional usage or require a very robust & extremely high-quality trimmer set, chances are a different (and more expensive) Wahl product is a better match. But if your goal is for a value set of trimmers that do a reasonably good job, this product is probably a good match, as they have worked very well for my needs.

Several years ago I purchased an air pot for the family as a way to have tea or coffee (french press) available all day. The air pot was by Palm restaurant if I remember correctly and I had purchased it at TJ Maxx around Christmas time. It lasted for only two years once we started using it more often in fall and winter. We didn't use it in summer at all.

The pot kept things hot for about five to six hours, and adequate but not great for tea overnight. The lever snapped off making it unusable.

I was worried after reading so many less than positive reviews on this, but decided to take a chance. I am SO glad I did!

APPEARANCE?
Although this air pot is not quite as nice looking as the stainless steel one we had before, the black is not bad. It does show smears and fingerprints more readily than the one we had before, so it has to be wiped down more often if that is an issue for you.

QUALITY OF COMPONENTS
Compared to the other air pots I have used including our own, this is what I would call more industrial in nature.
-The top lever has a nice spring to it.
-The inner lever that is used to apply pressure for the pump is quite sturdy in comparison and it snaps down nicely when not in use.
-The back hings opens on a spring which pulls down and the cover is in an open position.
-The pot does not close properly unless it is seated the way it should be in that hinge.
-The lock on the top is excellent. It has two buttons on either side.
-The liner came in perfect condition and the pump stick is well made and has a cushioned end as most do.
-The swivel on the bottom is also nice and works smoothly.
-The handle is very well made.

HOW DOES THIS AIR POT COMPARE TO MY EXPERIENCE?
I have to say that at first I was not sure what to expect. This air pot is a bit larger than the 1.7L that we had before, and I was not sure I would like the black. Once the water is inside, however, I have to say I am shocked at how long that the air pot keeps things HOT. We can get about 8-10 hours of truly HOT water out of this and I have emptied it three days later (it had been about half full) and the water was still very warm- not quite HOT, but still steaming. We plan our tea accordingly. When the water has been in there over six or seven hours, we move on to green teas or even white teas which take less hot water and it works like a dream. We don't have a temperature controlled pot.

I also use the hot water at times when I need to melt honey or something in water (for my iced tea) and it is not hot enough to use for hot tea. It is quicker than waiting for the hot water to come up if it has been a while and very convenient.

WHAT I LIKE ABOUT THIS AIR POT
-Strong lever on top
-Easy to use
-Hinge is secure
-Keeps hot a LONG time
-Swivel works nicely

WHAT I DON'T LIKE
-It takes two runs of our electric kettle which is 1.7L big to fill this air pot completely
-Black shows fingerprints easily

THE BOTTOM LINE
This air pot is well made. The components appear strong and have good performance with solid build to them. The contents if full when first put in the pot are kept HOT a REALLY long time and that makes it a pleasure to use. The top fits very securely and the pump seems to work very well, filling up an entire cup of tea in one pump if you don't press too hard all at once and are patient.

I am really glad that we purchased this pot and look forward to having it last a bit longer than our previous version. I have to say that it really has been a pleasure to use although it is a bit larger than I would like, on days when the whole family is crazy for tea or coffee, it is well worth having.

CAUTION
Just a warning- if you get this air pot on a very cold day, wait before you try to examine it. The two ball buttons on either side of the lid will not press in and you might be tempted to think that the unit is defective. I almost sent it back because it would not budge. I let it warm up really well in the house, and as soon as the plastic was warm, it functioned beautifully and we have not had an issue since.

I started in computers when we loaded the OS from reel-to-reel tapes. Then came the Tandy (Radio Shack) "PC" that loaded from cassettes. We often went on coffee breaks waiting for programs to load. We all knew that computers would be faster some day but I don't think any of envisioned something like the Samsung 850 EVO 250 GB M.2 SSD. This drive is really sensational. Certainly beats the 8" floppies we once used! I was lucky when I selected a Gigabyte GA-Z97X-UD3H (Rev 1.2) motherboard as it comes with the pesky screw pre-installed to hold the drive in place. For those of you who are planning on purchasing this drive, it shouldn't be too hard to find the screw. Ace Hardware, if there is one near you, usually has a good selection of metric screws. If not, one of the big box stores often have the right size. It shouldn't be too hard to find locally. Installing the drive couldn't be much easier. Just slip it into place and replace the screw. These are small screws so don't over tighten it. I was using this drive in a new build with the above mentioned motherboard (and I really like it), an Intel i7 4790k processor, and 32 GB of RAM. I also have two 1 TB Western Digital drive in raid for data storage (the SSD is only for the OS and programs that must be installed on the C: drive. When I build a new system or replace a boot drive I always rebuild the system. Migrating the system often brings along obsolete software or drivers that can eventually cause problems. I also have a WD 4 TB drive for long term data storage. I'm not telling you about the hardware to brag, it is just to give you an idea of the components working with the 850. I am using Windows 7 Ultimate and the system boots almost instantly. A friend timed it at 7 seconds. Takes me much longer to type in my 21 character password (I'm not paranoid, I just like long passwords) than it takes the system to boot. This drive is silent, doesn't vibrate, runs cool, and is just schmookin' fast. Saving data happens faster than it takes to press the "Save" icon.

Probiotics are live bacteria and yeasts that are good for you, especially your digestive system. We usually think of these as germs that cause diseases. But your body is full of bacteria, both good and bad. Probiotics are often called "good" or "helpful" bacteria because they help keep your gut healthy.

Ask your doctor if taking probiotics is a good idea for you. In general, probiotic foods and supplements are thought to be safe for most people, though some people with immune system problems or other serious health conditions shouldn't take them.

In some cases, mild side effects might include an upset stomach, diarrhea, gas, and bloating for the first couple of days after you start taking them. They may also trigger allergic reactions. Stop taking them and talk to your doctor if you have problems.

I was trying to choose. Sony MDR-V6 Sony MDR-7506, ATH-M30, ATH-M40... I looked at everything. I found a youtube channel, which plays direct from CD sample, then crossover in sync to various model headphones resampling the sound from the each headphone as it's placed over a foam head. - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sj69-mWHV3E - The point is, they are trying to reproduce what is heard. Also, I found another youtube channel of a guy who shows various headphones sampled through a graphic analyzer, showing the frequency response.

All headphones add something to the signal. So what you hear on one model isn't the same, with another. But of all the head phones, the ATH-M40x was identical in sound reproduction to the original music. You couldn't tell the difference. Why is this important? Two reasons, if you are an audio engineer, you will have a truer sound, what you hear, is what you will get. It goes both ways, what you listen to, will be what the sound engineer intended for you to hear.

For music with base, it has good presence, and you can hear details that sound muddy on other head phones. I have been listening to a lot of head phones. You do understand muddy and clarity, once you hear it.

With that said, and having spent some time, in store sampling, (note: I must say that the Sonys are really good too. I tried and liked the MDR-V55 as well. It's a DJ headset so it's a bit more base. I felt they were very clear and better than the MDR-X05 hands down.)

The ATH-M40x, has removable cables. They are field repairable. And you can choose between three different cables, although two come in the box.

They are son tested and approved. Now I have to keep them locked up, joking. They are well built. Some say the ATH-M50x is better. It's also said the M50x sound the same as last year's model, and the M40x sound as good as last year's M50 model too. Which is it? The M40x is specifically flat sounding for audio engineering. The M50x is targeted for the audiophile, with a V shape EQ. The M40x is in the sweet spot, unless you have money to burn.

I have purchased a number of HM-10 Bluetooth boards for various projects and half of them have been "fakes". (Fakes have unknown firmware that does not implement the command set of a true HM-10 board.) These boards are the real deal. I quick check using a terminal program to send AT commands shows that it is the official firmware load. The AT+VERS? command returned a version of v550 for the firmware and checking a few of the AT commands that are supposed to be supported in that version shows that they all appears to function as expected. The only difference between these boards and the other "real" HM-10s I have is the LED on the carrier board is blue in this version where it is red in the other ones.

Some HM-10 boards come with 6 pins for the connection and these come with just 4. (VCC, GND, TXD, RXD). The other two connections that don't have pins attached are EN and STATE. The holes are present in the carrier board, so you can add pins to these connections if you need to toggle the "ENable" or use the connection "STATE" as an input to something else.
